title: Eisenstein-ball factor base and norm-bounded (pi-adic) descent in Z[omega]
surface: 2(a) structured factor base + 2(e) special arithmetic of p, via the CM ring rather than the t-adic shape
hypothesis: Since p = 1 mod 3 splits in Z[omega] (class number 1) as p = pi*pibar with pi computable by Cornacchia from 4p = L^2 + 27M^2, the reduction Z[omega] -> Z[omega]/pi = F_p sends the hexagonal ball B_H = {alpha : N(alpha) <= H^2} onto a factor base of size ~H^2 that is exactly stable under the curve's automorphism x -> beta*x. If a Semaev relation among B_H elements can be forced to hold in Z[omega] and not merely mod pi, norm bookkeeping replaces the descent step and the relation becomes an exact char-0 identity attackable by lattice enumeration.
nongeneric_structure: The ring structure of F_p as Z[omega]/pi together with the j=0 CM automorphism: multiplication by omega is an ISOMETRY of the Eisenstein lattice, so the reduction of a norm-ball is simultaneously (i) a rank-2 lattice-structured subset of F_p and (ii) exactly closed under the curve's mu_6 automorphism group (beta*(a+b*beta) = -b + (a-b)*beta). This coincidence exists only for D=-3 curves. It is not a re-encoded generic search because the factor base is defined by the SIZE of a char-0 lift of the x-coordinate, a notion no generic-group algorithm can express.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] Semaev 2004, 'Summation polynomials and the discrete logarithm problem on elliptic curves' (ePrint 2004/031) introduced S_m. [ESTABLISHED] Silverman ~1999 'The xedni calculus and the ECDLP' (Designs Codes Cryptogr.) lifted POINTS to char 0 and died because global points of small height are governed by Mordell-Weil rank; Jacobson, Koblitz, Silverman, Stein, Teske ~2000 'Analysis of the xedni calculus attack' quantified the failure. DIFFERENT HERE: nothing is lifted to a global CURVE and no rank hypothesis is used; only x-coordinates are lifted to Z[omega], and the success condition is the weak numerical one N(S_m(x_1..x_m)) < N(pi) = p rather than the existence of a global point. [ESTABLISHED] GLV (Gallant-Lambert-Vanstone, CRYPTO 2001) already uses Z[omega] on the EXPONENT side; this idea uses it on the COORDINATE side.
smallest_experiment: PARI-GP, toy curves y^2=x^3+7 over p = 1 mod 3, 20-40 bits, prime order (ellcard/isprime loop; a 24-bit example found here: p=16777723, n=16773667). (1) Compute pi by qfbsolve/Cornacchia on 4p = L^2+27M^2 and verify Z[omega]/pi = F_p by mapping omega -> beta. (2) For H = p^(1/8), p^(1/6), p^(1/4), p^(1/3), build B_H as the image of the norm-ball; check experimentally that B_H is closed under x -> beta*x (it must be) and record |B_H|. (3) Enumerate triples in B_H and count (a) S_3 = 0 mod p, (b) S_3 = 0 exactly in Z[omega]. Subtract the trivial mu_6 orbits {alpha, beta*alpha, beta^2*alpha}, which I verified give S_3 = 0 identically. (4) Compare count (a) against the random prediction |B_H|^3/p to detect any excess.
kill_criteria: DEAD if, for every H with |B_H| >= p^(1/3): (i) the number of EXACT Z[omega] identities beyond the trivial mu_6 orbits is zero, and (ii) the mod-pi relation count agrees with |B_H|^3/p to within a factor of 2 (no structural excess). Secondary kill: measured cost per relation >= |B_H|^(m-1), i.e. no better than enumerating the factor base. Analytic kill already in hand: carry-free/norm-bounded exactness forces |B| ~ p^(1/deg S), and deg S_3 = 4 > 2, deg S_4 = 12 > 3, so the necessary condition |B| >= p^(1/m) fails and the gap WIDENS with m; only the bounded-quotient relaxation below can survive.
expected_complexity: Best case ~p^(1/3) group-equivalent operations (index calculus with m=3 and |B| = p^(1/3)), which would beat 2^127.8. This requires BOTH: (1) the relaxed condition S_m = pi*gamma with N(gamma) <= Gamma (bounded quotient, not exact zero) to admit solutions at density >= |B|^m/p, and (2) a lattice/enumeration method that finds such (x_1..x_m) in time much less than |B|^(m-1). Neither is established; my own degree analysis says the exact (Gamma=1) version cannot work.
novelty_note: Not xedni: no global points, no Mordell-Weil rank condition, no lifted curve. Not Weil descent: there is no subfield, the 'descent' is replaced by archimedean norm bookkeeping in the CM order. The specific new observation is that the Eisenstein norm-ball is simultaneously the natural 'small' set for char-0 lifting AND exactly the mu_6-stable set, so the factor base and the automorphism compression are compatible for free.

title: mu_6-invariant regrading of Semaev systems and measured first-fall degree over a prime field
surface: 2(b) extra relations from j=0/lambda + 2(d) symmetry reduction by the 6-fold automorphism group
hypothesis: For j=0 the symmetry group of the relation-search system is mu_6 semidirect S_m rather than {+-1} semidirect S_m, and S_m is weighted-homogeneous with wt(x)=1, wt(b)=3 (verified: every monomial of S_3 has weighted degree 4). Rewriting the system in mu_3-invariants (monomials of x-degree divisible by 3) and using the weighted grading to dehomogenize removes one variable and block-diagonalizes the Macaulay matrix into 3 character blocks; if this lowers the first-fall/solving degree enough, Groebner-based relation search over F_p could drop below the |B|^(m-1) enumeration cost.
nongeneric_structure: The j=0 CM automorphism acting on x-coordinates as x -> beta*x with beta^3 = 1 in F_p, plus the weighted grading of the Weierstrass model. Concretely verified here: S_3(x, beta*x, beta^2*x) = 0 IDENTICALLY in Z[beta]/(beta^2+beta+1). This is coordinate-level structure (a symmetry of the polynomial system, not of the abstract group), so it is not a generic-group operation; but note the honest flip side, also established here: that identity is just P + phi(P) + phi^2(P) = O, so lambda contributes exactly the mu_6 ACTION and no independent new relation among x_i (S_4(x, beta*x, x3, x4) degenerates to S_3(beta^2*x, x3, x4)).
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] Faugere, Perret, Petit, Renault, EUROCRYPT 2012, 'Improving the complexity of index calculus algorithms in elliptic curves over binary fields'; Faugere, Gaudry, Huot, Renault, 'Using symmetries in the index calculus for elliptic curve discrete logarithms' (J. Cryptology, ~2014) - both exploit the S_m symmetry and the [-1] symmetry over EXTENSION fields and obtain polynomial, not exponential, gains. [ESTABLISHED] Petit-Quisquater, ASIACRYPT 2012, 'On polynomial systems arising from a Weil descent' - first-fall degree heuristic. [ESTABLISHED] Duursma-Gaudry-Morain, ASIACRYPT 1999, 'Speeding up the discrete log computation on curves with automorphisms' - the automorphism group only buys sqrt(6) in rho, which is the constant-factor baseline this idea must beat. SEARCH: 'Petit Kosters Messeng algebraic approaches elliptic curve discrete logarithm prime fields PKC 2016' - expected to report that prime-field Semaev systems have solving degrees making the approach worse than generic. DIFFERENT HERE: the mu_3 grading is available only for j=0 and is absent from every one of those works (random curves over F_2^n).
smallest_experiment: Toy p of 20-32 bits, y^2=x^3+7, prime order. For m=3 and m=4 build the relation system S_(m+1)(x_1..x_m, x_R)=0 with a factor base condition, in two encodings: (A) raw x_i; (B) mu_3-invariant coordinates (e.g. e_i of the beta-orbit, or monomials of degree = 0 mod 3) plus the dehomogenized weighted grading. Compute a degree-graded Macaulay matrix in pure Python/numpy over F_p (or msolve/F4 if installable; gp's polresultant suffices for m=3) and record: the degree of first rank fall, the solving degree, and total field operations. Repeat over increasing p and fit cost = p^c.
kill_criteria: DEAD if the fitted exponent c is >= (m-1)/m for both encodings (no better than enumerating the factor base), OR if the mu_6-invariant encoding lowers the first-fall degree by at most 1 and the operation count by less than 6x (i.e. it only reproduces the known automorphism constant factor). Also DEAD if the first-fall degree is observed to grow with log p at all, since that alone implies an exponential cost.
expected_complexity: Realistically a constant-to-polynomial improvement only. A genuine asymptotic win would require the solving degree to be bounded independently of log p, which would be extraordinary; I do not expect it. Stated honestly: no complexity win is claimed unless the measured solving degree is O(1) in log p.
novelty_note: Not a restatement of FGHR: those works symmetrize under S_m and [-1] over extension fields where the descent already supplies the linear structure. Here the descent is absent and the mu_3 grading (a j=0-only feature) is being asked to do algebraic work on its own. Its main value may be a clean NEGATIVE: measuring that even the largest available symmetry group leaves prime-field Semaev systems at enumeration cost.

title: S_4 as a rank-4 bilinear form: relation search is orthogonality search, and the sum-membership oracle
surface: 2(a) factor bases with algebraic structure + 2(c) alternative resultant strategy, driven by an explicit resultant identity
hypothesis: Verified here: S_4 = (<u,v>^2 - D(u)D(v))/4 where u=(A,B,C) are the z-coefficients of S_3(x1,x2,z), <u,v> = B1B2 - 2A1C2 - 2A2C1, D = B^2-4AC, and D(u) is always a square in F_p when x1,x2 are x-coordinates of rational points (so sqrt(D) is computable). Hence S_4 = 0 is exactly a rank-<=4 BILINEAR condition Phi(w(x1,x2), w(x3,x4)) = 0 with w = (A,B,C,sqrt(D)) in F_p^4. Relation search is therefore an orthogonality-pair search, and the substitute for descent is a factor base B whose image variety {w(x1,x2) : x1,x2 in B} is algebraically describable, so that intersecting it with a hyperplane can be SOLVED rather than enumerated.
nongeneric_structure: An explicit classical resultant identity for the summation polynomials of the x-line, plus the rationality of sqrt(disc) forced by the fact that x(P1+P2) and x(P1-P2) both lie in F_p. Both are coordinate-level facts about F_p, invisible to a generic algorithm; the attack quantity is the geometry of the image of B x B in F_p^4, i.e. the interaction between a coordinate-defined set and the group law.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] Semaev 2004 for S_m and the resultant recursion. [ESTABLISHED] The m=4 case is well known to be 'just' a collision/meet-in-the-middle (S_4 = 0 iff P1 +- P2 = +-(P3 +- P4)), which is why it gives nothing for generic factor bases - this is the standard dead end. DIFFERENT HERE: making the rank-4 bilinear form explicit turns the vague hope 'maybe some factor base helps' into a single measurable requirement (a fast sum-membership oracle / non-random image variety), and supplies a cheap statistical test for it. [ESTABLISHED, and a hard constraint I want to record] If B has SMALL sumset in the group, then B is essentially a generalized arithmetic progression of known multiples of a known point, the search degenerates to a knapsack in Z/n, and Shoup's generic bound (Shoup, EUROCRYPT 1997) applies - so B must be coordinate-structured with a large group-sumset but computable incidence.
smallest_experiment: Toy curve, 20-28 bits. For each candidate B of size ~p^(1/2) or p^(1/3) - (i) the Eisenstein ball of idea 1, (ii) an interval, (iii) a coset of the small multiplicative subgroup of order dividing p-1, (iv) small t-adic digits - compute: (1) |{x(P+P') : P,P' in B}| versus |B|^2 (Freiman-type collapse test); (2) linear algebra over F_p on all monomials of degree <= 6 in the 4 coordinates of w to test whether any nontrivial polynomial vanishes on the image {w(x1,x2)}, beyond the obvious ones; (3) wall-clock time to find an orthogonal pair using sort/hash on a 2-coordinate projection versus brute force over pairs.
kill_criteria: DEAD if for every candidate B: |{x(P+P')}| = |B|^2 (1-o(1)); the only polynomials of degree <= 6 vanishing on the w-image are the trivial ones implied by the definitions of A,B,C,D; and no search strategy beats N^2 pair enumeration. That outcome kills not just this idea but the entire 'structured factor base over a prime field' family, which is why it is worth running first.
expected_complexity: A win requires a sum-membership oracle answering 'is x(P+P') in T?' in time much less than |B| per query. With such an oracle at cost |B|^delta, relation search costs |B|^(1+delta) per relation and total |B|^(2+delta) with |B| = p^(1/3), i.e. p^((2+delta)/3), which beats p^(1/2) iff delta < 1/2. That is the precise condition; nothing currently suggests it holds.
novelty_note: The identity S_4 = (<u,v>^2 - D(u)D(v))/4 is classical invariant theory of binary quadratics applied to Semaev polynomials, and I verified it numerically here; I have not seen it used to phrase ECDLP relation search as a rank-4 orthogonality problem. Its value is that it converts a vague surface into one falsifiable measurement.

title: The lattice crossing exponent E(m) vs m: a decisive test for interval and lattice factor bases
surface: 2(a) intervals/lattice-defined subsets + 2(c) alternative (lattice, not Groebner) solving strategy
hypothesis: For an interval or lattice-box factor base, relation finding is 'find a small root of S_(m+1)(x_1..x_m, x_R) = 0 mod p in a box of side H'. Write S = sum_j A_j(x_1..x_m) x_R^j; because the integer coefficients of S_m are tiny (verified: 1, 2, 4, 28 for S_3) and S_m is weighted-homogeneous of weighted degree d_m, one gets |A_j| <= H^(d_m - j). The vector (A_j) lies in a lattice of covolume p, so a lattice attack can isolate the relation only when the box volume H^E(m) is <= p, where E(m) = sum_j (d_m - j) over 0 <= j <= deg_{x_R} S_(m+1). Relation existence needs H^m >= p. The whole family is alive iff E(m) <= m for some m.
nongeneric_structure: The integer lift of S_m with tiny coefficients, plus the additive/metric structure of F_p (the notion of 'small residue'). A generic group has no notion of size, so this is genuinely non-generic; it is not a re-encoded generic search because the lattice acts on coefficient vectors of a fixed integer polynomial, not on group elements.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] Coppersmith 1996 (small roots of modular polynomials); Jochemsz-May, ASIACRYPT 2006, 'A strategy for finding roots of multivariate polynomials with new applications to cryptanalysis'; Coron's bivariate integer variants. [ESTABLISHED] No general Coppersmith result exists for dense bivariate MODULAR equations, which is precisely the case here. SEARCH: 'Semaev 2015 new algorithm for the discrete logarithm problem on elliptic curves ePrint 2015/310' - expected to propose prime-field factor bases of restricted x-coordinates with heuristic solution counts. SEARCH: 'Kosters Yeo notes on summation polynomials' - expected to show those heuristics fail and the final step degenerates to random search. DIFFERENT HERE: rather than arguing about unproven heuristics, compute one exponent inequality exactly and settle the family. Partial result already in hand: d_3 = 4 with deg_{x_R} = 2 gives E(2) = 9 >> 2; d_4 = 12 with deg_{x_R} = 4 gives E(3) = 50 >> 3, so the gap widens rapidly.
smallest_experiment: (1) In PARI-GP compute S_4, S_5, S_6 for b=7 by iterated polresultant, read off the weighted degree d_m and deg_{x_R}, and evaluate E(m) for m <= 6-8 (minutes of work; exact, no curve needed). (2) On toy curves of 24-40 bits, implement Jochemsz-May shift lattices for f(x1,x2) = S_3(x1,x2,x_R) mod p with LLL (fpylll or a plain Python LLL), plant a known small solution by choosing x_R = x(P1+P2) for x1,x2 in the box, and measure the largest exponent e such that H = p^e still allows recovery. Repeat for S_4 with three unknowns.
kill_criteria: DEAD if E(m) > m for all m <= 8 (the exact symbolic computation settles this in an afternoon) AND the measured recoverable exponent e stays <= 1/4 while relation existence needs e >= 1/m. I expect exactly this outcome; the value of the experiment is that it closes the interval/lattice branch of surface 2(a) with a number rather than a hunch.
expected_complexity: No win unless E(m) <= m for some m, in which case relation finding costs poly(log p) per relation and the total becomes ~p^(1/m) - a genuine break. The honest statement is that E(2)=9 and E(3)=50 already make this look hopeless, and the experiment is a falsification exercise.
novelty_note: Not a new lattice technique; the novelty is reducing an entire folklore-dead-end family to a single computable exponent inequality, with the exact weighted degrees of S_m (which I verified for S_3 and derived for S_4 via the resultant identity) as the input.

title: Descent along p = t^8 - t - 977 (t = 2^32): carry-free Weil restriction to Z, and the exact reason it breaks
surface: 2(e) the special shape of p: F_p as a quotient of Z[T]/(T^8 - T - 977) at T = 2^32
hypothesis: F_p is the image of R = Z[T]/(T^8 - T - 977) under T -> 2^32. Take a factor base of x-coordinates with bounded t-adic digits, x = sum_{j<8} c_j t^j with |c_j| <= B. Because S_m has tiny integer coefficients, the lifted value is an element of R; if no carries occur (all 8 reduced coefficients stay below t/2), then S_m = 0 mod p forces all 8 coefficients to vanish over Z. One congruence mod p becomes 8 integer equations in the digits - the exact structural analogue of Weil restriction, with Z (via the SNFS polynomial) in place of the subfield F_q.
nongeneric_structure: The literal shape p = 2^256 - 2^32 - 977, i.e. p = f(t) for a degree-8 integer polynomial f with tiny coefficients and t = 2^32. This is the SNFS representation of p. It is not a generic search re-encoding because the factor base is defined by the digit expansion of a field element, a property of the representation of F_p, not of the group.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] SNFS uses exactly this representation of special p for integer factorization and for DL in F_p^*. [ESTABLISHED] Gaudry (JSC 2009) and Diem (Compositio 2011) need a genuine subfield for the descent; Z is here playing the role of the 'subring at infinity'. As far as I know this transfer to summation polynomials is unpublished. [HEURISTIC, derived and partly MEASURED here] The carry-free regime is narrower than it looks: reduction mod T^8 - T - 977 amplifies coefficients by up to 977^3 ~ 2^30 (three reduction rounds for a degree-28 expansion) plus the monomial count, and I measured that for t = 2^32 even digits bounded by 1 produce reduced coefficients of ~2^39 > t/2. General law: carry-free descent yields |B| ~ p^(1/deg S_(m+1)), while index calculus needs |B| >= p^(1/m); since deg S_3 = 4 > 2 and deg S_4 = 12 > 3, the requirement fails and the gap WIDENS with m.
smallest_experiment: Toy special primes p = t^k - t - c with k = 2,4,8 and t = 2^8..2^16 chosen so p is prime, p = 1 mod 3 and #E(y^2=x^3+7) is prime (PARI ellcard). (1) Sweep the digit bound B and, for random triples with digits <= B, compute the lifted S_3 in Z[T], reduce mod f(T), and record the maximum reduced coefficient versus t/2 - i.e. measure the true carry-free threshold B*(t,k,c) and hence |B| = (2B*)^k as a power of p. (2) Compare against the predicted p^(1/deg S) law. (3) Test the one loophole: restrict the digit SUPPORT to a sparse set of slots chosen so that 4-fold sums of slot indices are distinct modulo the reduction relation (a B_4/Sidon condition), so products land in distinct t-slots without carries despite larger digits; measure the largest resulting |B|. (4) Also test whether choosing a different polynomial representation of the same p (smaller |c|, different k) improves the threshold.
kill_criteria: DEAD if the measured carry-free |B| is <= p^(1/4) for S_3 and <= p^(1/12) for S_4 across all (k, t, c) and all sparse-support configurations (confirming the law), and if no Sidon-support configuration reaches |B| >= p^(1/m) for the corresponding m. A B_4 set inside 8 (or even 256) slots has size ~k^(1/4), giving a factor base of size ~2^4 - if the experiment confirms this, the loophole is closed too. Additional kill: the bounded-carry relaxation (allow g(t) = k*p with |k| <= K) reduces to ONE integer equation rather than 8, i.e. it carries no more information than the original congruence - if measured relation-finding cost there matches brute force, the whole surface-2(e) branch is dead.
expected_complexity: For a win one needs a carry-free (or provably-bounded-carry) regime with |B| >= p^(1/m) and a solver for the resulting 8 integer equations in 8(m-1) small digit unknowns running in time much less than |B|^(m-1). The first requirement already appears unsatisfiable by the measured degree law; I claim no complexity win.
novelty_note: Not Weil descent (no subfield) and not xedni (no global points). The specific contributions are the transfer of the SNFS polynomial representation to Semaev relation-finding, the measured 977^3 carry amplification, and the |B| ~ p^(1/deg S) versus p^(1/m) gap law, which appears to be the crisp reason the whole 'special shape of p' surface cannot substitute for descent.

title: Z[omega]-indexed elliptic nets: the rank-2 exponent lattice as a substitute for descent
surface: 2(b) j=0 / lambda structure, pushed to the exponent side via elliptic divisibility sequences instead of summation polynomials
hypothesis: Summation polynomials are index-blind: they say a set of points sums to zero but carry no information about discrete logarithms. Elliptic nets do carry it. For CM by Z[omega] there is a rank-2 elliptic net W : Z[omega] -> F_p satisfying quadratic (Somos-type) recurrences, and GLV gives k = k1 + k2*lambda with |k1|,|k2| ~ sqrt(n). Expanding k1,k2 in base 2^e and using the net recurrences as polynomial relations in the digit variables turns the ECDLP into a sparse quadratic system over F_p. If its solving degree is bounded independently of log n, the search is solved rather than enumerated - the 2-dimensional index lattice playing the role that the n F_q-coordinates play in Weil descent.
nongeneric_structure: The elliptic divisibility sequence / elliptic net attached to E and P: a coordinate-level, characteristic-0-defined divisibility structure whose values in F_p are computable from division polynomials, combined with the CM Z[omega]-module structure that makes the net rank 2 rather than rank 1. A generic-group algorithm cannot even WRITE this system down, since it has no access to the field values W(k); that is precisely why Shoup's bound does not formally forbid it.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] Lauter and Stange, SAC 2008, 'The elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem and equivalent hard problems for elliptic divisibility sequences' - they proved equivalences between ECDLP and EDS problems but obtained no speedup. [ESTABLISHED] Stange, 'Elliptic nets and elliptic curves' (Algebra & Number Theory, ~2011) and her thesis, which define higher-rank nets and their recurrences. SEARCH: 'Shipsey thesis elliptic divisibility sequences Royal Holloway 2001' - expected to give the double-and-add style net computation used here. DIFFERENT HERE: prior work used rank-1 EDS indexed by Z; the rank-2 net indexed by Z[omega] matches the GLV lattice exactly, so digits are half-length and the system is 2-dimensional, which is the closest structural analogue of descent's multi-coordinate linear structure. [SPECULATION] that the resulting quadratic system has a low solving degree - this is the entire bet and it is unsupported.
smallest_experiment: Toy CM curves y^2 = x^3 + 7 over p = 1 mod 3, 20-32 bits, prime order, in Python/PARI. (1) Build the rank-1 EDS from division polynomials and verify the Somos-4 recurrence W(m+n)W(m-n) = W(m+1)W(m-1)W(n)^2 - W(n+1)W(n-1)W(m)^2. (2) Extend to the Z[omega]-indexed net using lambda and verify the rank-2 recurrences numerically. (3) For a known k, set up the digit system with e = 2 and 3 (so 2*ceil(log_2(sqrt(n))/e) unknowns), and measure with a small Groebner/Macaulay implementation over F_p: the first-fall degree, the solving degree, the number of spurious solutions, and total operations, as p grows from 20 to 32 bits. Fit cost = p^c.
kill_criteria: DEAD if the measured solving degree grows linearly in log p (which immediately implies cost >= p^(1/2)), OR if the system is underdetermined with ~p^(1/2) spurious solutions per target, OR if the fitted exponent c >= 0.5 over the 20-32 bit range. Any of these three means the net encoding is just a re-encoded generic search, which is the honest prior expectation.
expected_complexity: A win requires the solving degree to be O(1) in log p, giving poly-time or at least subexponential solving of the digit system; then the ECDLP would fall in roughly the cost of one Groebner computation on O(log n / e) variables. Nothing supports this; the kill criteria above are designed specifically to detect the re-encoding failure mode quickly.
novelty_note: Not a restatement of Lauter-Stange (they proved equivalence of hard problems and used rank-1 sequences over Z). The new element is aligning the net's index ring with the CM order Z[omega] so that the index lattice is 2-dimensional and matched to GLV, making the digit system half as deep. It is the only idea here that attacks the exponent side while still living on the summation-polynomial/divisibility-relation surface, and it is included mainly because the other five all bottom out on the same obstruction: over a prime field there is no subring of F_p to descend to.

title: Interval/GAP factor base + skewed multivariate Coppersmith on j=0 summation polynomials
surface: Index calculus over prime-field elliptic curves
hypothesis: Relation finding over a factor base {P : x(P) in a generalized arithmetic progression} is exactly 'find small roots of S_{m+1}(x_1..x_m,x_R) = 0 mod p'; the CM weighted-homogeneity of S_m for j=0 plus deliberately SKEWED (unbalanced) boxes may push multivariate Coppersmith past the balanced-box bound far enough to solve the constrained system in time p^{1/m} per relation.
nongeneric_structure: Two at once: (i) the field/integer structure of F_p — an interval or GAP has Euclidean (lattice) structure, which by Freiman/Green-Ruzsa is the ONLY kind of intermediate-size structured subset of F_p once multiplicative subgroups are unavailable (verified unavailable here: p-1 = 2*3*7*13441*P237, largest usable divisor ~2^20.7); (ii) the CM/j=0 structure: S_3 for y^2=x^3+b is weighted-homogeneous of weighted degree 4 (wt x = 1, wt b = 3), so the relation variety is invariant under x_i -> beta*x_i, letting one quotient by Z/3 and work with ratios, cutting lattice dimension.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] Semaev 2004 'Summation polynomials and the discrete logarithm problem on elliptic curves' introduces S_m and explicitly poses solving S_m = 0 with x_i in a prescribed interval as the open problem for prime fields. [ESTABLISHED] Gaudry 2009 (index calculus for abelian varieties) and Diem 2011 (On the DLP in elliptic curves) solve the analogous constrained system over F_{q^n}, n>1, because 'x in F_q' is a LINEAR condition after Weil restriction; no such descent exists over F_p. [ESTABLISHED] Coppersmith 1996/97 and Howgrave-Graham 1997 give the small-root machinery; the balanced heuristic bound for a polynomial of degree d per variable is roughly prod X_i <= p^{1/d}, while relations need prod X_i ~ p, and deg_{x_i} S_{m+1} = 2^{m-1}, so the gap widens with m. WHAT IS DIFFERENT: prior treatments assume balanced boxes and the full polynomial; here the Z/3 CM symmetry is used to dehomogenize (reducing the number of free variables by one), the boxes are skewed (X_1 >> ... >> X_m with prod X_i = p) with the largest variable enumerated/sieved rather than lattice-solved, and the equation is reformulated over Z as S(x) = k*p with |k| small, turning it into a polynomial-value-hits-a-fixed-prime problem where the Newton polytope (not the total degree) governs the lattice. SEARCH: 'summation polynomial Coppersmith small roots prime field index calculus' — expect either nothing, or a note that the achievable bound is off by a power.
smallest_experiment: Toy curves y^2 = x^3 + 7 over primes p = 1 mod 3 of 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40 bits with prime group order (generate with PARI/GP: forprime + ellinit + ellcard, keep prime orders). For m=2 (S_3 with x_3 = x_R fixed) implement Howgrave-Graham/Coppersmith with PARI's qflll (already installed) over shift polynomials of S_3 and its beta-dehomogenized quotient; empirically determine gamma_max(p) = the largest gamma such that roots with x_1,x_2 <= p^gamma are recovered, over >=200 random instances per size. Repeat with skewed boxes (X_1 = p^{a}, X_2 = p^{1-a}) sweeping a in [0.1,0.9], and for m=3 with S_4. Compare gamma_max against the requirement gamma = 1/m. Cross-check every 'root' against a brute-force enumeration so success is unambiguous.
kill_criteria: DEAD if measured gamma_max <= 1/(2m) (i.e. no better than the classical balanced Coppersmith bound) and does not increase with p over the six sizes; DEAD if the skewed variant never beats the balanced one; DEAD if every recovered relation is one that a straightforward enumeration over the smaller box would have found in less wall-clock time. Also DEAD if, for the best observed gamma, the implied per-relation cost exceeds p^{1/m} by a factor that grows with p.
expected_complexity: If multivariate Coppersmith could be made to work at prod X_i ~ p with per-variable degree 2^{m-1}: factor base p^{1/m}, per-relation solve poly(log p), sparse linear algebra p^{2/m}; needs m >= 5 to beat rho, giving ~p^{2/5} = 2^102. Requires the (currently false) claim that the lattice determinant condition can be met at the full box size — i.e. that the Z/3 symmetry plus skew buys a factor 2^{m-1} in the exponent.
novelty_note: Not a restatement of 'Semaev over prime fields is hard': the textbook dead end is stated for balanced boxes and the unmodified polynomial. The concrete new levers are the j=0 weighted-homogeneity quotient (specific to CM D=-3 curves like secp256k1, absent for generic a,b) and the skew/sieve hybrid with the integer reformulation S = k*p, which changes which lattice is built, not merely the framing.

title: Hunting a computable proxy for the Z[omega]-norm: a 4-query reduction from ECDLP to any height oracle
surface: Index calculus over prime-field elliptic curves (factor base = points of small CM height)
hypothesis: E(F_p) is Z[omega]/(pi-1), a quotient of a EUCLIDEAN ring, so a 'small generating set' and a height DO exist (GLV coordinates); the only missing ingredient for a factor base of small-height points is an efficiently computable membership/height test. If ANY statistic of the affine coordinates (x,y) in F_p has even epsilon-correlation with the norm form N(a+b*omega) = a^2-ab+b^2 of the GLV representation, ECDLP falls in ~epsilon^{-2} group operations.
nongeneric_structure: The coordinate representation in F_p (integer size, digit structure, continued-fraction/rational-reconstruction profile, residue characters) combined with the CM lattice: End(E) = Z[omega] acts F_p-rationally via (x,y)->(beta x, y), and E(F_p) is a Z[omega]-module of rank 1, so every point has a canonical short representative a+b*omega with |a|,|b| ~ sqrt(n). A generic-group adversary sees opaque encodings and provably has no such statistic; the whole question is whether the F_p-coordinate encoding leaks the lattice position.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] Gallant-Lambert-Vanstone 2001 give the short Z[omega]-representation; it is exactly why rho gains sqrt(6) on secp256k1. [ESTABLISHED] Shoup 1997 shows no generic algorithm can do better than sqrt(n), which is precisely the statement that the encoding must be used. [ESTABLISHED/folklore] the standard obstruction quoted against elliptic index calculus is 'no notion of smallness on E(F_p)' — but that is an assertion about the COMPUTABILITY of the height, never a theorem; no paper I am confident of has systematically measured correlation between coordinate statistics and GLV height. WHAT IS DIFFERENT: I can state an exact, elementary reduction rather than a vague hope. Given an oracle h(P) returning N of the short representative, write Q = (a+b*omega)G; then h(Q - cG) = (a-c)^2 - (a-c)b + b^2 is a MONIC quadratic in c, so two values of c give 2a-b, and two queries along the omega-direction (Q - c*psi(G)) give 2b-a, hence a and b: 4 queries, no search. A noisy/biased statistic can be substituted by least-squares fitting the same quadratic over many c. SEARCH: 'statistical bias x-coordinate discrete logarithm elliptic curve GLV height correlation' — expect only negative folklore.
smallest_experiment: Curves y^2 = x^3+7 over 20-32 bit primes p = 1 mod 3 with prime order n. Brute-force the full discrete log table (feasible to 2^32 in C). For each point compute the exact short GLV pair (a,b) by reducing the log against the lattice generated by (n,0) and (-lambda,1) (PARI qflll). Then compute a battery of statistics on (x,y): x as an integer; Hamming weight of x; min over d <= D of |x*d mod p| (rational reconstruction); first partial quotients of x/p; the cubic residue character chi_3(x) and chi_3(y) (CM-natural: chi_3(y) is invariant under both negation and psi, so it is a function on the exact orbits rho quotients by); quadratic characters chi(x-r) for random r; the smoothness of x as an integer. Measure empirical mutual information and the R^2 of a least-squares fit of the monic quadratic c -> statistic(x(Q-cG)) against the true N(a-c+b*omega), over 10^5 random Q and c in a window of size p^{0.4}. Also directly test whether chi_3(y(P)) is equidistributed over the sparse set {P : N(a+b*omega) <= B} for B = n^{0.2}, n^{0.3}, n^{0.4}.
kill_criteria: DEAD if mutual information between every statistic and log2 N(alpha) is below the sampling noise floor (estimated by permuting labels) AND does not grow with p across four sizes; DEAD if the quadratic-fit R^2 is statistically indistinguishable from zero; DEAD if chi_3(y) is equidistributed on the small-norm sets to within the Weil-type error p^{-1/2}*|set|^{1/2}.
expected_complexity: With an exact oracle: O(log p) group operations (4 queries + arithmetic). With an epsilon-biased statistic and independent noise: ~epsilon^{-2} log p evaluations, i.e. any epsilon >= 2^{-60} would break secp256k1. Requires that the bias be real and not an artifact of small-p effects — so the scaling across sizes is the whole test.
novelty_note: The usual dead end is 'points have no height'. This inverts it: the height exists and is canonical (Z[omega] is Euclidean); only its computability is in doubt, and that is an empirical question with a cheap decisive measurement plus an exact 4-query reduction making any positive signal immediately catastrophic. A clean negative result is itself the sharpest quantitative form of the 'no Euclidean structure' folklore.

title: Dickson/torus factor base: the one intermediate-size ALGEBRAIC subset of F_p that secp256k1 actually admits
surface: Index calculus over prime-field elliptic curves
hypothesis: Lang-Weil forbids positive-dimensional algebraic factor bases over F_p, but a zero-dimensional one of intermediate size exists when a sparse high-degree polynomial has many F_p-roots. For secp256k1, p+1 = 2^4 * 7322137 * 45422601869677 * Q184, so the norm-1 torus T <= F_p2^* has subgroups of order d ~ 2^45.4, 2^49.4, 2^68.2, 2^72.2; the trace set S_d = {t + t^{-1} : t^d = 1} is a subset of F_p of size d/2 cut out by the single equation D_d(x,1) = 2 (Dickson), with O(log d) membership test by Lucas ladder. Relation search becomes a mixed system (Semaev = additive on the curve) + (Dickson = multiplicative on the torus); the hypothesis is that resultant/Groebner elimination against the SPARSE constraint solves it in time o(d^{m-1}).
nongeneric_structure: Field structure of F_p and of F_p2 (norm-1 torus, Dickson/Lucas recurrences), plus the arithmetic of p+1 for this specific prime, plus Semaev's summation polynomials (algebraic geometry of the curve). The condition 'x in S_d' is a genuine polynomial condition of degree d with a fast straight-line program — the prime-field stand-in for the subfield condition 'x in F_q' that makes Gaudry/Diem descent work.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] Gaudry 2009 and Diem 2011: descent index calculus needs the factor base to be an algebraic subset of intermediate size, available over F_{q^n} (n>1) as a subfield/linear subspace. [ESTABLISHED] Lang-Weil 1954: over F_p an absolutely irreducible variety has either O(1) or ~c*p points, so no bounded-degree positive-dimensional factor base exists — the standard reason 'index calculus does not apply to prime fields'. [ESTABLISHED] Petit-Quisquater 2012 and Faugere-Gaudry-Huot-Renault 2014 study exactly how the Groebner cost of Semaev-plus-constraint systems scales, and how symmetries reduce it. [ESTABLISHED, sum-product] Bourgain-Glibichuk-Konyagin 2006 and related work show additive and multiplicative structure in F_p are maximally incompatible — the main theoretical reason to expect this to fail. WHAT IS DIFFERENT: the standard dismissal only considers subgroups of F_p^*, which for secp256k1 are numerically unusable (p-1 = 2*3*7*13441*P237, largest usable divisor 2^20.7 — I verified this). Using the TORUS of order p+1 instead, via the trace/Dickson parameterisation, restores usable sizes on the actual target curve, and Dickson polynomials add a composition tower D_{de} = D_d o D_e plus O(log d) evaluation, so the constraint never has to be expanded as a dense degree-d polynomial. SEARCH: 'Dickson polynomial factor base elliptic curve index calculus prime field' and 'norm-one torus factor base ECDLP' — I expect no hit; if there is one it should report the same sum-product obstruction.
smallest_experiment: Pick toy primes p = 1 mod 3 of 24-44 bits such that (a) #E(F_p) for y^2=x^3+7 is prime and (b) p+1 has a divisor d near p^{1/3}, p^{1/4}, p^{1/5} (search with PARI factorint over a few thousand candidate p). Build S_d by enumerating g^i + g^{-i} for a generator g of the order-d subgroup of the norm-1 torus in F_p2 (PARI ffinit/ffgen). For m=3 and m=4, solve {S_{m+1}(x_1..x_m,x_R)=0, D_d(x_i)=2} by (i) pure enumeration (baseline, cost ~ (d/2)^{m-1}) and (ii) elimination: PARI polresultant of S against the Dickson constraint, with the Dickson step done by Lucas-ladder modular composition instead of dense expansion; optionally msolve (standalone, no Magma/Sage) for a Groebner baseline. Fit log(solve time) = alpha*log(d) + const across at least five values of d spanning a factor 2^8, separately for m=3,4.
kill_criteria: DEAD if the measured exponent alpha is >= m-1 - 0.1 (i.e. the algebraic solve is no better than enumerating (m-1)-tuples) for both m=3 and m=4; DEAD if solve time is dominated by an unavoidable output of size ~d per eliminated variable (the degree-blowup regime), since then alpha >= m-2 and the total index-calculus cost stays >= p as computed by the standard accounting; DEAD if relation YIELD deviates below the heuristic d^m/p by more than a constant factor, which would indicate the torus set is correlated with the curve in a way that suppresses solutions.
expected_complexity: Best case: factor base d ~ p^{1/m} with m=5 (d ~ 2^51 — and 2^49.4 really is a divisor of p+1 for secp256k1), per-relation solve d^{o(1)}, sparse linear algebra d^2 = p^{2/5} => ~2^102. This holds only if elimination against the sparse Dickson constraint avoids the degree blow-up, i.e. if the constrained solve is quasi-linear in d rather than d^{m-2}. Sum-product heuristics predict it does not.
novelty_note: The textbook dead end is 'no algebraic set of intermediate size exists over F_p'. That is true for positive-dimensional sets (Lang-Weil) but false for sparse zero-dimensional ones; the usual multiplicative-subgroup instantiation is killed for secp256k1 by the factorization of p-1, and the torus/Dickson instantiation — which survives numerically, as I checked — appears not to have been tried. It also gives a concrete, cheap first deliverable for the real curve: the p+1 factorization above is exactly the search for usable d.

title: Relation search as a low-weight-codeword problem: Riemann-Roch evaluation vectors, Plucker collisions, and ISD/representation techniques
surface: Index calculus over prime-field elliptic curves (relations from divisors of low-degree functions)
hypothesis: m points of E(F_p) sum to O iff their Riemann-Roch evaluation vectors v(P) in L(m*O)^* are linearly DEPENDENT, so relation finding over a factor base of size N is exactly 'find m linearly dependent columns among N explicitly known columns in F_p^m' — a minimum-weight-codeword problem with a KNOWN parity-check matrix. Information-set-decoding with representations (BJMM-style) might beat the N^{m-1} birthday count that every elliptic index calculus is stuck at.
nongeneric_structure: The explicit F_p-coordinates of points: v(P) = (1, x, y, x^2, xy, ...) is computable, so the parity-check matrix is known WITHOUT knowing any discrete logarithm. This is the crucial asymmetry versus the naive 'relation lattice', which has determinant n but unknown entries (they are the DLPs). Also uses Riemann-Roch on the curve and, for m=3, the fact that the third intersection of a line with the cubic is -(P+Q).
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] The divisor/function view of relations is the standard framework of index calculus in high-genus Jacobians (Adleman-DeMarrais-Huang; Enge-Gaudry) and fails for genus 1 because all places have degree 1, so there is no smoothness gradation. [ESTABLISHED] Wagner 2002 (generalized birthday) and Howgrave-Graham-Joux 2010 / Becker-Joux-May-Meurer 2012 (representations) beat birthday bounds, but all require either a filtration compatible with the group operation (absent in a prime-order group) or an explicit matrix. [ESTABLISHED] Shoup 1997 forbids progress from the group operation alone. WHAT IS DIFFERENT: the reformulation makes the matrix explicit, so ISD is at least well-posed; moreover, two-sided splitting can be phrased as a subspace-intersection problem whose test is BILINEAR in Plucker coordinates (two (m/2)-subspaces of F_p^m meet nontrivially iff the pairing of their Plucker vectors vanishes), turning 'find a dependent m-set' into 'find a zero inner product between two lists' where fast-matrix-multiplication and 3SUM-style techniques become available. For m=3 the problem literally is 3SUM on a cubic curve. SEARCH: 'minimum weight codeword elliptic curve relation index calculus information set decoding' and 'collinear triples cubic curve finite field subquadratic' — expect no direct hit; if there is one it should report an Omega(N^2)-type barrier.
smallest_experiment: Toy curves of 20-36 bits, prime order. Fix N = p^{1/(m-1)} random factor-base points, build the m x N matrix of evaluation vectors, and compare three relation-finding algorithms on identical instances: (i) baseline enumeration of (m-1)-subsets; (ii) Prange/Stern/Dumer-style ISD adapted to F_p with target weight m (implement in C or Python+gmpy2); (iii) the Plucker formulation with a hash/meet-in-the-middle on partial inner products. Measure the empirical exponent beta in time ~ N^beta for m = 3, 4, 5 across at least five values of N per curve size, and verify each found dependency really is a group relation (sum of the m points = O) as a correctness check. Also measure the density of solutions to confirm the N^m/p heuristic.
kill_criteria: DEAD if beta >= m-1 - 0.05 for all three algorithms and all m tested, i.e. no measurable subquadratic (for m=3: sub-N^2) behaviour; DEAD if ISD's advantage vanishes as p grows at fixed N/p^{1/(m-1)} (a small-p artifact); DEAD if the Plucker meet-in-the-middle cannot be made to hash on anything better than a 1/p-probability scalar condition, since then its cost is provably L^2/p * L^2-type with no gain.
expected_complexity: Even a perfect solver needs m >= 5 to beat rho (linear algebra N^2 = p^{2/m}). Best case: an ISD exponent beta = (m-1)*(1-delta) with delta > 0 would give total p^{max(2/m, 1 - delta*(m-1)/m)}; with m=5 and delta >= 0.2 this lands near p^{2/5} = 2^102. Requires ISD to help in the extreme regime weight = codimension = m with N >> m, which is exactly where ISD is usually weakest.
novelty_note: The textbook dead end says 'relations among factor base points require knowing their discrete logs, or come for free from a random function but then the points are random'. The reformulation sidesteps the first horn: the dependency matrix is explicit and DLP-free, which is precisely the object ISD needs. The idea is not a re-encoded generic search because the matrix entries are affine coordinates in F_p, invisible to a generic adversary.

title: Xedni restricted to the CM/Mordell family: measure the lift density that Jacobson-Koblitz-Silverman-Stein-Teske predicted, in the one family where the lift is canonical
surface: Index calculus over prime-field elliptic curves (lifting to characteristic 0)
hypothesis: Xedni died because imposing congruence conditions forced the lifted curve to behave like a random curve of rank ~0-1, so the probability that several prescribed points lift simultaneously to small height was essentially 1/p. secp256k1 is special: y^2 = x^3 + 7 is ALREADY a global curve with CM by Z[omega], so lifts stay in the one-parameter Mordell family y^2 = x^3 + k, k = 7 mod p, where ranks are tabulated, can be large, and Mordell-Weil is a Z[omega]-module (halving the number of independent generators needed). The hypothesis is that the effective lift density in this constrained family is measurably better than the random-curve model.
nongeneric_structure: Lifting to characteristic 0 plus the CM structure: j = 0 is preserved under the lift, so the lifted curve automatically has CM by Z[omega], its Mordell-Weil group is a Z[omega]-module, and canonical heights of omega-conjugate points are equal — so a rank-r Mordell-Weil group supplies 2r 'directions' at the same height, and the lattice of relations after reduction is a Z[omega]-lattice amenable to Euclidean reduction.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] Silverman 1999 'The xedni calculus and the elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem' (Designs, Codes and Cryptography). [ESTABLISHED] Jacobson, Koblitz, Silverman, Stein, Teske ~2000 'Analysis of the xedni calculus attack' shows the success probability is essentially p^{-1}-ish: Mestre's method cannot be inverted usefully, and the congruence conditions destroy the rank advantage. [ESTABLISHED] canonical height counting: #{P in E(K) : h(P) <= H} ~ H^{r/2}, so a factor base of size p^{1/m} needs height ~p^{2/(m*r)} and coefficients that are astronomically large unless r is huge. WHAT IS DIFFERENT: xedni allowed the curve to move over a 5-parameter family and then asked for small rank obstructions; here the family is 1-parameter and the lift is canonical (j = 0 forced), so the experiment actually becomes feasible and the relevant statistic (rank and small-height point count of y^2 = x^3 + k for k in a fixed residue class mod p) is directly measurable with PARI's ellrank/ellheegner — no Magma needed. Being honest: I expect this to confirm the random model, and the key structural objection is already visible — global relations among independent global points do not exist, so the reduction lattice is still only obtainable from discrete logs.
smallest_experiment: Toy primes p of 20-30 bits with y^2 = x^3 + 7 of prime order. For k running over 7 + j*p, j = 1..10^4, compute in PARI/GP: rank (ellrank), the number of points of naive height <= H for H = 10^3..10^6 (ellratpoints or a direct search over x = a/d^2), and the multiset of their reductions mod p. Measure (i) the distribution of ranks in the class k = 7 mod p versus a control class; (ii) the number of distinct points of E(F_p) hit by small-height global points, versus the random model prediction; (iii) whether hits concentrate on any structured subset (e.g. small GLV norm — cross-check with the cm-height-oracle-probe tables). Then attempt the actual xedni step: prescribe 4-6 target points in E(F_p) and count how many j in a bounded range give a lift with all of them of height <= H.
kill_criteria: DEAD if the rank distribution in the residue class k = 7 mod p is statistically indistinguishable from the control class; DEAD if the number of prescribed points that simultaneously lift to height <= H matches the random model p^{-(#points - dim of family)} to within a constant factor; DEAD if the reductions of small-height global points show no bias toward small GLV norm (Kolmogorov-Smirnov against uniform).
expected_complexity: No credible complexity win unless ranks in the constrained family are systematically large (r >> 10) AND the reduction lattice can be written down without discrete logs. If both held, the DLP would reduce to a CVP in a Z[omega]-lattice of dimension r and determinant n, giving roughly n^{1/r}-flavoured costs — but the second condition is exactly what I expect to be false, so this is a measurement, not a projected attack.
novelty_note: This is an acknowledged dead end proposed only in a strictly narrowed form: the CM/Mordell family, where the lift is canonical rather than Mestre-engineered and where the Z[omega]-module structure changes the height-counting exponent. The deliverable is a quantitative replication of the JKSST probability argument in the one family relevant to secp256k1, which to my knowledge was never done for j = 0 specifically.

title: Sparse-limb factor base tuned to p = 2^256 - 2^32 - 977, attacked by bit-level constraint propagation
surface: Index calculus over prime-field elliptic curves
hypothesis: Because 2^256 = 2^32 + 977 mod p, reduction mod p is a shift-and-add that raises 'limb weight' by at most one, so the set S_w = {x : at most w nonzero 32-bit limbs} is an intermediate-size set (|S_3| ~ 2^102) that is nearly stable under multiplication by powers of 2 and has an extremely compact bit-level description. The hypothesis is that S_{m+1}(x_1..x_m,x_R) = 0 mod p restricted to x_i in S_w has enough carry-level structure for a CP/SAT solver to find relations in time far below |S_w|^{m-1}.
nongeneric_structure: The special shape of p (a sparse pseudo-Mersenne prime) together with the binary representation of F_p elements: the modular reduction is a near-free bit operation, and the factor base is defined by the 2-adic digit pattern, a structure that exists only because of this specific p. Semaev's polynomials supply the algebraic relation on top.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] SAT/algebraic-cryptanalysis attacks on ECDLP exist and are uniformly hopeless when the search space is the full group; the encoding of field multiplication blows up. [ESTABLISHED] Semaev 2004 for the relation equation. [ESTABLISHED] Wagner 2002 does NOT apply: the k-list technique needs the group operation to respect a bit filtration, and E(F_p) has prime order with no such filtration — which is why the constraint must be imposed on x-coordinates via the polynomial, not on group elements. WHAT IS DIFFERENT: prior SAT attempts encode an unconstrained DLP; here the solver is given a tiny, heavily constrained search space (w limbs nonzero) and a modulus whose reduction costs almost no clauses, so the propagation has something to bite on. SEARCH: 'SAT solver summation polynomial elliptic curve relation search pseudo-Mersenne' — expect nothing, or negative results on unconstrained encodings only.
smallest_experiment: Construct toy primes of the same shape at 24-48 bits (p = 2^k - 2^j - c, prime, = 1 mod 3, with y^2 = x^3+7 of prime order; search with PARI). Define limbs of 6 or 8 bits so that |S_w| ~ p^{1/3}. Encode S_3(x_1,x_2,x_R) = 0 mod p (m=2) and S_4 (m=3) as bit-level CNF/CP with the sparse reduction expressed as a shift-add, and run a modern CP or SAT solver (kissat/cadical, pip-free standalone builds) against a C brute-force baseline over S_w^{m-1}. Measure solver time and conflicts as a function of |S_w| over at least five sizes and fit the exponent. Sanity-check that solutions returned are genuine group relations.
kill_criteria: DEAD if solver time scales as |S_w|^{m-1} or worse (i.e. no better than brute force) across the size sweep; DEAD if conflict counts grow super-linearly in the number of limbs, indicating no useful propagation; DEAD if the solver cannot even certify UNSAT on instances where brute force proves no relation exists, within 100x the brute-force time.
expected_complexity: Best case, if CP solving were polynomial in the number of limbs: factor base p^{1/m}, per-relation cost poly(log p), linear algebra p^{2/m}, so ~p^{2/5} = 2^102 for m=5. This requires the (highly implausible) claim that carry-level propagation defeats the algebraic rigidity of Semaev's polynomial; I include it because it is the only idea here that uses the actual shape of secp256k1's prime and it is cheap to falsify decisively.
novelty_note: Not a generic re-encoding: the search space is the same one Coppersmith would attack, but the solver exploits carry structure rather than lattice structure, and the factor base is defined by the digit pattern relative to this specific sparse p — a property no other 256-bit curve shares in the same way. Its main value is as a cheap independent check on the idea that the interval/GAP factor base is unsolvable by ANY technique, not just lattices.

title: Recover the DL as the cotangent scalar alpha mod pi (the other half of the Eisenstein CRT)
surface: 3 (j=0 / CM by Z[omega]); coordinate-side realization of End(E) = Z[omega]
hypothesis: For a j=0 curve the DL k is the image of a SHORT Eisenstein integer alpha = a+b*omega under the ring map Z[omega] -> Z/n (omega -> lambda); the image of the SAME alpha under the other ring map Z[omega] -> F_p (omega -> beta), c = a + b*beta mod p, determines k outright. I verified this: from c alone, 2D lattice enumeration returns <= 6 candidates and always contains the true k (40/40 trials on 24/32/40/48/56-bit toy curves). So ECDLP on secp256k1 is equivalent to computing ONE field element that lives on the coordinate side (it is the scalar by which the endomorphism alpha acts on the invariant differential dx/y and on the formal group), which is a different attack target than k and is exposed to lattice / p-adic / Coppersmith-style methods that an opaque group element is not.
nongeneric_structure: End(E) = Z[omega] gives TWO ring homomorphisms out of Z[omega]: reduction mod (pi-1) (= the group action, what a generic algorithm sees) and reduction mod pi (= the action on the cotangent space at O, where omega acts by the explicit constant beta in F_p because omega: (x,y)->(beta x, y) sends dx/y to beta dx/y). The second map is invisible to a generic algorithm: it is a property of the coordinate representation, not of the abstract group. Also CM-specific: the automorphism omega makes the canonical (n-torsion / Serre-Tate) lift of any point to E(Z/p^m) computable in O(1) group ops, by correcting a lift until omega~(P~) = [lambda]P~ (the defect lies in the formal group and scales by beta - lambda mod p).
prior_work: Satoh-Araki 1998, Semaev 1998, Smart 1999 ('The discrete logarithm problem on elliptic curves of trace one') break anomalous curves by lifting to Z/p^2 and using the formal-group logarithm; that works only because n = p puts the instance INSIDE the formal group. Silverman's xedni calculus (DCC 2000) and its demolition by Jacobson-Koblitz-Silverman-Stein-Teske ('Analysis of the xedni calculus attack', DCC 2000) lift POINTS to characteristic 0 and die on height/rank. What is different here: I do not lift the point and I do not need a global model. The target is the tangent-space invariant of the ENDOMORPHISM alpha (equivalently its degree N(alpha) = a^2-ab+b^2, recoverable from c by Cornacchia), which is a 256-bit quantity with a 2-dimensional lattice structure, not a rank/height object. SEARCH: 'elliptic curve discrete logarithm' + 'GLV decomposition' + 'action on invariant differential' / 'endomorphism degree oracle' — I am not aware of this reduction being stated, and it should be checked for prior art before investing.
smallest_experiment: Already partially run; scripts are in the repo. (i) /home/user/virtualaquarium/ecdlp/py/cm_cotangent_check.py: loads data/curves_special.json (24-56 bit y^2=x^3+7 curves with prime order), computes the GLV short rep (a,b) of a random k by 2D Gauss reduction of {(a,b): a+b*lambda = 0 mod n}, forms c = a+b*beta mod p, then recovers k from c ALONE by enumerating the coset of {(a,b): a+b*beta = 0 mod p} inside |(a,b)|^2 <= 1.5n. Result: 100% recovery, mean 4.7 / max 6 candidates. (ii) The open half: build a 'null battery' of every cheaply computable functional of (P,Q) over Z/p^2 — the omega-eigen (canonical) lift tau(P), the naive integer-representative lift, their formal-group difference d(P) in F_p, tangent slopes, the discrepancy of the group law computed over Z with carries — and measure mutual information with c over >= 2^20 samples per curve. (iii) Decisively: verify computationally that E~(Z/p^m) splits as Z/n (+) Z/p^(m-1) with BOTH projections computable in poly time without knowing k (the omega-trick above gives the projection in O(1)).

Also DEAD (for the statistical route) if every functional in the null battery has empirical mutual information with c below the 3-sigma sampling floor at 2^20 samples on >= 10 toy curves. title: Explicit CM in characteristic 0: measure whether the Weber/ray-class route can ever cost less than n
surface: 3 (explicit CM theory: canonical lift to Q(omega), Weber function x^3, ray class field of conductor (pi-1))
hypothesis: Because h(-3)=1, E is the reduction of the fixed global CM curve y^2=x^3+7 over Q(omega), and E(F_p) is the reduction of its (pi-1)-torsion; the Weber values x(T)^3 generate the ray class field of conductor (pi-1) over K=Q(omega), in which pi splits completely (pi = 1 mod (pi-1)) — which is exactly why all x-coordinates are in F_p. So the DLP is the problem of matching an element of F_p to its complex CM counterpart. nongeneric_structure: Main theorem of complex multiplication for K=Q(omega) with class number 1, Weber function h(x,y)=x^3 for j=0, complete splitting of pi in the ray class field of conductor (pi-1), and the analytic uniformization C/Z[omega] in which the discrete log is the position of the torsion point in the fundamental hexagon. title: Volcano depth from the CM conductor: secp256k1 has thousands of small-degree F_p-isogenies; search those encodings
surface: 3 (isogeny class / volcano structure forced by the CM norm equation 4p = t^2 + 3v^2)
hypothesis: The conductor of Z[pi] inside Z[omega] is v, where 4p = t^2 + 3v^2. I computed for secp256k1: t = 432420386565659656852420866390673177327 and v = 303414439467246543595250775667605759171 = 3 * 79 * 349 * 2698097 * 1359580455984873519493666411. For every l | v, Frobenius acts as the SCALAR t/2 on E[l], so all l+1 order-l subgroups are Galois-stable and all l+1 l-isogenies are F_p-rational. Hence secp256k1 has 4 rational 3-isogenies, 80 rational 79-isogenies, 350 rational 349-isogenies and 2698098 rational 2698097-isogenies, and roughly 2^38 curves of the SAME group order n reachable by feasible-degree isogenies. Hypothesis: among these ~2^38 explicitly computable coordinate encodings of the same cyclic group, one has exploitable structure (unusually small-height j, a coordinate distribution admitting a factor base, or a cheaper point-decomposition).
nongeneric_structure: The l-isogeny volcano depth at l equals v_l(v), and v comes from the CM norm equation — pure CM data, not group data. The 'Frobenius is a scalar on E[l] when l | v' phenomenon (which makes ALL l+1 isogenies rational rather than 0 or 2) is specific to non-maximal Z[pi] inside a CM order. Transferring the DLP along an isogeny changes the coordinate encoding while preserving the abstract group — the very thing a generic algorithm cannot do.
prior_work: Kohel's 1996 thesis and Fouquet-Morain 2002 for volcano structure; Velu 1971 and Bernstein-De Feo-Leroux-Smith (sqrt-Velu, ANTS 2020) for computing the isogenies; Jao-Miller-Venkatesan, 'Do all elliptic curves of the same order have the same difficulty of discrete log?' (ASIACRYPT 2005) shows (under GRH, via expander mixing) that DLP difficulty is uniform ON AVERAGE inside an isogeny class. What is different: JMV is an averaging/random-self-reducibility statement; the question here is whether a RARE structured encoding exists in an explicitly enumerable, CM-determined, and rather small reachable set — and the CM data tells you exactly which set. Honest counterweight: every reachable curve has j != 0, hence Aut = {+-1}, so rho on it is sqrt(6) SLOWER; the null hypothesis predicts a measurable loss, not a gain.
smallest_experiment:
Toy curves y^2=x^3+7 of 24-40 bits. PARI: compute t, v = sqrtint((4p-t^2)/3), factor v (tools/cm_recon.gp already does this). For each l | v, compute the eigen-subgroups of E[l] (roots of the l-division polynomial) and build all l+1 isogenies with Velu, pushing P and Q through; verify #E' = n and that the DL is preserved. Then, over the whole reachable class, measure: (a) minimum integer height of j', (b) empirical rho cost (reuse csrc/rho.c via lib/librho.so) on each curve, (c) number of points of

with x < p^(1/2) and with x in any low-degree algebraic set, (d) Semaev S_3/S_4 decomposition success rate per curve.
kill_criteria: DEAD if across all reachable curves on >= 10 toy curves: min height of j' is within 1 bit of the random-uniform expectation, every measured rho cost is >= the j=0 baseline (i.e. the predicted sqrt(6) loss and nothing else), and no coordinate statistic (a)-(d) deviates by more than 3 sigma from the random-curve control. Additionally DEAD for secp256k1 specifically if the reachable class size (product over feasible l | v of (l+1)) is below 2^40 while the probability of any usable structure per curve is below 2^-40.
expected_complexity: No asymptotic claim. A hit would only be interesting if it produced a factor base, which would then put prime-field index calculus in play (L_p(1/2) at best, and nothing rigorous). Best case realistically: a constant-factor or a definitive negative.
novelty_note: The concrete fact that secp256k1's CM conductor v factors as 3*79*349*2698097*(95-bit prime), and therefore that the curve is NOT isogeny-isolated over F_p at small degree, is computed here rather than assumed; most treatments stop at 'h(-3)=1 so the horizontal graph is trivial', which is true and hides the depth-1 descending structure that actually supplies the alternative encodings.

title: mu_6-invariant summation polynomials: run Semaev decomposition in the Weber coordinate u = x^3
surface: 3 (Aut(E) = mu_6 acting on the x-line by x -> beta x; invariant ring generated by x^3) crossed with index calculus
hypothesis: Semaev's summation polynomials S_m are symmetric but, on a j=0 curve, they are additionally invariant under the free mu_3-action x_i -> beta x_i (and under x_i -> x_i with y -> -y). They therefore descend to polynomials S~_m in the invariants u_i = x_i^3 (equivalently y_i^2 = x_i^3+b), cutting the degree in each variable by a factor 3. Hypothesis: this degree drop lowers the degree of regularity of the point-decomposition system enough to change the empirical solving exponent, and if prime-field index calculus is ever feasible with a bounded-coordinate factor base, j=0 curves are where it shows up first.
nongeneric_structure: The order-3 automorphism group of a j=0 curve acting on coordinates (x,y) -> (beta x, y) with beta in F_p, and the fact that the quotient of E by <omega> is the rational curve y^2 = u + b so that the Aut-invariant coordinate is exactly the Weber function u = x^3. This is algebra on the coordinates of the model, invisible to a generic algorithm; it is also strictly more than the known sqrt(6) rho speedup, which only uses the action on the SET of points and not on the polynomial systems.

Symbolic Comput. 2009); Diem, 'On the discrete logarithm problem in elliptic curves' (Compositio 2011). Symmetry exploitation: SEARCH: 'Faugere Gaudry Huot Renault using symmetries in the index calculus for elliptic curves discrete logarithm Journal of Cryptology 2014' and SEARCH: 'symmetrized summation polynomials small order torsion points index calculus Faugere Huot Joux Renault Vitse' — those use symmetries from 2-torsion / rational torsion translations over EXTENSION fields; what is different here is a free mu_3 automorphism action whose invariant is a single cube, applicable over the prime field, and giving a 3^m rather than 2^m degree reduction. kill_criteria: DEAD if the u-coordinate system does not reduce the observed maximum intermediate degree by roughly the predicted factor (3 per variable), OR if the fitted solving exponent in the u-system is statistically indistinguishable from the x-system, OR if the decomposition probability over the bounded factor base stays at the trivial (|F|/p)^(m-1) level so that the total relation-collection cost extrapolates to >= n^(1/2) group operations even with free solving.

title: Cubic residue character of the x-coordinate: hunt for an exact CM (Jacobi-sum) evaluation instead of square-root cancellation
surface: 3 (Hecke Grossencharacter of Z[omega] attached to E; cubic/sextic residue symbols on coordinates)
hypothesis:
On secp256k1, beta is NOT a cube mod p (verified: beta^((p-1)/3) != 1; also p = 7 mod 9, 7 is neither a square nor a cube mod p). Hence chi_3(x(omega P)) = chi_3(beta) * chi_3(x(P)) — the cubic character of the x-coordinate is mu_3-EQUIVARIANT, not invariant. Since the L-function of a j=0 curve is attached to a Hecke Grossencharacter of Q(omega), certain character sums on CM curves have EXACT Gauss/Jacobi-sum evaluations rather than merely square-root bounds. Hypothesis: some sum over

mixing chi_3 of the x-coordinate with a multiplicative or additive test character has an exact CM evaluation whose value depends on k (or on the GLV pair (a,b)) modulo a small integer, leaking log bits per query.
nongeneric_structure: The cubic residue symbol in F_p together with the CM relation #E = p+1-t with t expressed by Jacobi sums for y^2 = x^3 + b (classical; Ireland-Rosen ch. 18), plus the equivariance chi_3(beta) != 1 which is a property of this specific p and beta. Character values of coordinates are a coordinate-side computation; a generic algorithm has no access to chi_3(x(P)).
prior_work: Ireland & Rosen, 'A Classical Introduction to Modern Number Theory', ch. 18 (point counts on y^2=x^3+b via Jacobi sums) [ESTABLISHED]. SEARCH: 'Kohel Shparlinski exponential sums elliptic curve points ANTS 2000' and Shparlinski's later work on character sums over points of elliptic curves — the expected content is square-root cancellation bounds, i.e. a strong prior that no exploitable bias exists. What is different: those are upper bounds for generic curve/character combinations and they do not rule out an EXACT evaluation for the specific pair (cubic character on x, mu_3-equivariant CM action) on a curve whose L-function is a Hecke character; and the cost of settling it empirically is hours.
smallest_experiment:
24-40 bit toy curves. Enumerate the full cyclic group

(feasible up to ~2^26 with the C library in lib/librho.so or plain Python for 2^20), tabulate s_j = chi_3(x(jP)) as an element of mu_3 (one modular exponentiation per point, or a precomputed cubic-residue table). Then: (1) DFT of (s_j) over j and look for peaks above the sqrt(N) noise floor; (2) correlate s_j with j mod m for m = 2..64 and with the GLV coordinates (a_j, b_j) mod m; (3) test whether s_{j} * s_{j'} * conj(s_{j+j'}) has a non-uniform distribution (a cocycle bias); (4) repeat over >= 30 curves and both choices of beta and lambda. Also test the sextic character chi_6 and the quadratic character of y.
kill_criteria: DEAD if every correlation and every DFT peak is within 4 sigma of the i.i.d.-uniform null over >= 10^7 total samples across >= 10 curves, and the cocycle distribution in (3) is uniform to within sampling error. That is a decisive negative and closes the 'CM character leakage' idea family.
expected_complexity: If a bias delta existed and were constant, a distinguisher costs O(1/delta^2) group operations per leaked bit, hence poly-time DLP. The realistic outcome is delta = O(N^(-1/2)), i.e. nothing.
novelty_note: This is not the known automorphism-class trick (which uses x^3 as an invariant to fold orbits); it uses the fact that chi_3 is EQUIVARIANT rather than invariant, so it is a candidate 'partial logarithm in the lambda direction' — and it is settled decisively in hours, which is the right price for a long shot.

title: A Z[omega]-hermitian self-pairing: is the degeneracy on E(F_p) forced only by the alternating property?
surface: 3 (CM by Z[omega] and the sesquilinearity of the Weil pairing over Z[omega]); transfer maps
hypothesis: A computable self-pairing f with f([k]P) = f(P)^(k^2) into any group where DL is subexponential would break ECDLP (take a square root mod n). CM is exactly the setting where self-pairings are known to exist and to break schemes (isogeny-based class-group actions). On secp256k1 the naive construction dies because omega acts on E(F_p) as the SCALAR lambda, so the lambda-eigenspace is isotropic: e(P, omega P) = e(P,P)^lambda = 1, and more generally e(alpha P, Q) = e(P, conj(alpha) Q) forces e = 1 on E(F_p) x E(F_p). Hypothesis to test: whether some Z[omega]-hermitian or cubic (rather than alternating) analogue of the Weil/Tate pairing exists whose degeneracy is NOT forced by antisymmetry, and whether any small m with m | gcd(n, p^k - 1) gives a usable reduced Tate pairing.
nongeneric_structure: Z[omega]-sesquilinearity of the Weil pairing (e(alpha P, Q) = e(P, conj(alpha) Q)) and the decomposition of E[m] into the two omega-eigenspaces E[mu] and E[conj(mu)] for split m; the fact that E(F_p) = ker(pi-1) is one full eigenspace. This is a CM statement about the module structure of torsion plus a pairing computation on coordinates (Miller functions), not a group-generic manipulation.
prior_work: Menezes-Okamoto-Vanstone 1993 and Frey-Ruck 1994 (MOV/FR transfers; blocked by embedding degree). SEARCH: 'Verheul evidence that XTR is more secure than supersingular elliptic curve cryptosystems Journal of Cryptology 2004' — expected content: distortion maps do not exist for ordinary curves, i.e. the scalar action is the obstruction. SEARCH: 'Castryck Houben Merz Mula Vercauteren weak instances of class group action based cryptography via self-pairings CRYPTO 2023' — expected content: explicit self-pairings built from CM endomorphisms that are nondegenerate precisely when the endomorphism does NOT act as a scalar on the relevant torsion. What is different: instead of re-deriving the known blockage, I ask the sharper question of whether the hermitian form (rather than the alternating form) can be nondegenerate on a single eigenspace, and I settle it both by proof and by direct computation.
smallest_experiment: 24-40 bit toy curves. (1) Implement Miller's algorithm for e_n over the smallest field where E[n] is rational and verify e_n(P, alpha P) = 1 for all alpha in Z[omega] up to norm 100 — confirming eigenspace isotropy numerically. (2) Compute the embedding degree: smallest k with n | p^k - 1, and gcd(n, p^k - 1) for k up to 10^4, on toy curves AND on secp256k1 (fast in PARI). (3) For every m dividing gcd(n, p-1) compute the reduced Tate-Lichtenbaum pairing t_m(P,P) and check whether it is nontrivial. (4) Brute-force search for any computable candidate f built from Weber values, division polynomials at P, and Miller functions, testing the quadratic law f(2P) = f(P)^4 on 10^4 random points.
kill_criteria: DEAD if (1) gives identically trivial pairings for every alpha (as the isotropy argument predicts), (2) gives gcd(n, p^k - 1) = 1 for all k <= 10^4 on secp256k1, and (4) finds no candidate satisfying the quadratic law beyond trivial constants. Any one of these alone is close to decisive; together they close the pairing/transfer family for j=0 ordinary curves.
expected_complexity: If a self-pairing into F_(p^k)^* with small k existed, DLP would fall to L(1/3) via number-field-sieve DLP in the target field. For secp256k1 the embedding degree is almost certainly enormous, so the realistic outcome is a confirmed impossibility.
novelty_note: Not a re-run of MOV: the question is whether the CM hermitian structure evades the alternating-form degeneracy that kills self-pairings on ordinary curves, which is precisely the property recent isogeny-crypto attacks exploit elsewhere. Cheap, and it converts a widely repeated 'pairings do not help here' into a checked statement with explicit numbers.

title: Digit-box factor base over O = Z[t]/(t^8-t-977): relation search as a small-solution polynomial system mod p
surface: 4(b) primary, 4(a) secondary — does F_p = Z[t]/(f(t), t-2^32) give a workable factor base?
hypothesis: Define the factor base as points whose x-coordinate lies in the image S_B of a coefficient box {sum a_i t^i : |a_i| <= B} under the ring surjection phi: O -> F_p, t -> 2^32. Because f is sparse with tiny coefficients, products and the (polynomial, Jacobian-coordinate) group law lift to O with controlled coefficient growth, so a k-fold decomposition R = P_1+...+P_k becomes a system of low-degree integer equations mod p in 8k unknowns each bounded by B. The hypothesis is that an LLL/Coppersmith/Groebner hybrid solves that small-solution system faster than meet-in-the-middle.
nongeneric_structure: The explicit ring presentation F_p = Z[t]/(f(t), t-2^32) with f = t^8-t-977 sparse and of tiny height (this is exactly the SNFS polynomial), plus the fact that the elliptic group law is a polynomial map with small integer coefficients in projective/Jacobian coordinates. Not a re-encoded generic search: candidate relations are produced by lattice reduction / Groebner elimination on an integer lattice defined by the lifted equations, never by walking in the group; the algorithm never queries the group oracle to find a relation, only to verify one.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] Semaev 2004 (eprint, 'Summation polynomials and the discrete logarithm problem on elliptic curves'); Gaudry 2009 (J. Symbolic Comput., 'Index calculus for abelian varieties of small dimension and the ECDLP'); Diem 2011 (Compositio, 'On the discrete logarithm problem in elliptic curves') — all give subexponential/index-calculus results ONLY over F_{q^n} with n growing, because the factor base is defined by an F_q-LINEAR (algebraic) condition that Weil restriction turns into a polynomial system. Over a prime field there is no subfield, so 'x is small' is an archimedean/lattice condition, not an algebraic one, and every published prime-field attempt collapses to birthday cost. SEARCH: 'Semaev 2015 eprint New algorithm for the discrete logarithm problem on elliptic curves' — should be a prime-field summation-polynomial proposal whose claimed complexity was never confirmed. SEARCH: 'Amadori Pintore Sala discrete logarithm prime-field elliptic curves Finite Fields Appl 2018'. [ESTABLISHED] Coppersmith 1996 small-root methods. WHAT IS DIFFERENT HERE: the digit condition is not an arbitrary interval — it is phi(box) for a ring homomorphism from an order whose multiplication has near-zero coefficient growth, so the lifted relation equations have small height and are genuine candidates for lattice small-root machinery. Also note (measured) f mod p has factor degrees [1,3,4], so O ⊗ F_p = F_p × F_{p^3} × F_{p^4}; Gaudry/Diem index calculus does apply to E(F_{p^3}), but at cost ~p^{4/3} >> p^{1/2}, and our target is a direct summand — embedding into a larger group never helps. That dead end is closed by this computation.
smallest_experiment: Toy primes of the same shape: p = m^8 - m - c with m = 2^5 (p ~ 2^40) and m = 2^6 (p ~ 2^48), c small, p = 1 mod 3, and #E(F_p) prime for y^2 = x^3+7 (search c with a 30-line Python/PARI script; the 16-bit case p = 4^8-4-113, n = 64921 is already verified working). For k = 2,3,4: PLANT a decomposition (sum k random digit-box points, call the sum R), then (i) measure MITM baseline cost, (ii) build the lifted system in O (Jacobian-coordinate addition chain, one quadratic per addition, unknowns = 8 digits per summand), (iii) run an LLL/Coppersmith lattice built from shifted monomials, and (iv) a Groebner/resultant solve (PARI polresultant for k=2,3; a small Buchberger or msolve for k=4). Measure the largest box product prod(X_i) at which the planted solution is actually recovered, and compare to the density threshold prod(X_i) ~ p at which solutions first exist.
kill_criteria: DEAD if, at the density where solutions first exist (prod of bounds ~ p), neither the lattice nor the algebraic solver recovers the planted decomposition for any k in {2,...,6} at 40 and 48 bits, AND the measured success threshold scales like p^{1/d} (d = total degree of the system) rather than p^{1-o(1)} — i.e. the 'Coppersmith deficit' is a positive power of p and does not shrink as bit-size grows. Also DEAD if the solver works only when the box is so large that MITM is cheaper.
expected_complexity: If relation finding were poly-time with |FB| = p^{1/k}, total cost is dominated by sparse linear algebra ~ p^{2/k} plus |FB| x (relation cost): k=6 gives ~2^{85}, k=8 gives ~2^{64}. For this to hold there must exist an algebraic solver for k-fold small-solution systems mod p at solution-density 1 — precisely the regime where all known Coppersmith-type methods fail by a factor p^{1-1/d}.
novelty_note: Not the textbook 'small-x factor base' dead end (which is killed by the counting argument |FB|^k >= p forcing a birthday test). The version here replaces TESTING membership in the factor base with SOLVING for it, using the specific order O attached to p's shape; the measurable deliverable is the exact size of the Coppersmith deficit for the elliptic relation system, a number nobody seems to have published for prime fields.

title: Quantifying and attacking the height gap: exponentially many small lifts for F_p^* vs polynomially many for E
surface: 4(a)/4(e) — what the elliptic analogue of SNFS would need, and the exact gap to attack
hypothesis: SNFS works because every element of F_p^* has ~2^B lifts of bit-size B and the S-unit group has rank |S| (unbounded) with log-height generators. For E the analogue fails by Siegel/Mordell-Weil: #{P in E(K): canonical height <= B} ~ c B^{r/2}, polynomial. Hypothesis to attack: rank inflation (fields where p splits completely, or the free degree-1 prime in K = Q[t]/(t^8-t-977)) can be pushed far enough that relations exist AND the mod-p vanishing condition correlates with the Neron-Tate height lattice enough for CVP/enumeration to find relations without solving a knapsack.

Not a generic search: relations would be found by lattice enumeration under the height quadratic form, an object invisible to a generic group oracle.
