[ESTABLISHED] Smart 1999 / Satoh-Araki 1998 / Semaev 1998: p-adic (formal group) attacks need trace 1. NEW PRECISE STATEMENTS I VERIFIED OR DERIVED HERE: (1) E(Q) = {O} exactly for y^2 = x^3+7 (PARI: analytic rank 0, trivial torsion, conductor 21168) — the 'rational side' of an elliptic SNFS is literally empty for secp256k1. (2) The family y^2 = x^3 + (7 + kp), k = 0,1,2,..., ALL reduce to secp256k1 mod p, so Mordell-Weil rank is not really the binding constraint — relations require many small points on ONE such curve, and since |b| ~ p forces minimal heights >= (1/3)log|b| ~ 59 nats while relations need points up to height ~ log p ~ 177 nats, the count (177/59)^{r/2} >= p forces rank r >= ~322, against a world record of ~29 (SEARCH: 'Elkies Klagsbrun 2024 elliptic curve rank 29' to confirm the current record). (3) [ESTABLISHED, and worth stating as a barrier] any attack factoring through the formal-group logarithm is vacuous when n != p: n is a p-adic unit, so the lift ambiguity n*p*Z_p equals p*Z_p and the induced homomorphism E(F_p) -> pZ_p/npZ_p is identically zero.
smallest_experiment: Two cheap measurements in PARI/GP, no Sage/Magma. (A) Rank-vs-height tradeoff: for d up to ~10^5 use ellrank/ellheegner on the quadratic twists of y^2=x^3+7 (i.e. y^2 = x^3 + 7d^3) restricted to d that are quadratic residues mod a toy p (so p splits completely in the multiquadratic field); record rank and the canonical height of each generator; fit the growth of minimal generator height vs d and check whether sum-of-ranks r(H) with height bound H ever satisfies H^{r/2} >= p before the heights blow past log p. (B) Equidistribution test of the relation condition: take a curve over Q of rank 3-5 with small generators (standard tables) and toy primes p of 10-20 bits so that (log p)^{r/2} >~ p; enumerate coefficient vectors c in the height-bounded region, mark those with sum c_i R_i = O in E(F_p), and test whether the marked set is a union of cosets / clusters at small height / has any lattice-detectable structure versus a Poisson model.

Also DEAD on arrival if any proposed variant routes through the p-adic logarithm, by the n != p collapse above.

title: CM/Heegner orbits as the only known source of exponentially many height-controlled points, and whether their discrete logs carry class-group structure
surface: 4(d)/4(e) — CM field, class numbers, and whether E(F_p) embeds in a number-field object with cheap relations
hypothesis: The ingredient the SNFS analogy lacks is a family of exponentially many points of bounded canonical height with a poly-size description. Heegner/CM points supply exactly that: for a discriminant D with the twist of E having analytic rank 1, the h(D) ~ sqrt(|D|) Galois conjugates of the Heegner point live in E(H_D), have comparable heights, are permuted simply transitively by Cl(D), satisfy Kolyvagin norm relations, and (if p splits completely in H_D, which is a Cornacchia-testable condition) reduce into E(F_p). Hypothesis: the map Cl(D) -> Z/n, [a] -> dlog(reduction of P_a), carries exploitable structure (affine-homomorphic behaviour, low Fourier support over Cl(D), or unexpected linear relations), which would give both a factor base and, unlike every other construction, a decomposition handle.
nongeneric_structure: CM theory: j = 0, End(E) = Z[omega] with D = -3, class field theory over ring class fields H_D, the Gross-Zagier/Kolyvagin Euler system, and the simply transitive Cl(D)-action. A generic group has no analogue of a canonical family of points indexed by a computable class group.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] Gross-Zagier 1986 (heights of Heegner points), Kolyvagin 1990 (Euler system norm relations), Hafner-McCurley 1989 (class groups of imaginary quadratic orders in L[1/2], so Cl(disc) here is computable in ~2^40 ops). SEARCH: 'Jetchev Kane equidistribution of Heegner points ternary quadratic forms' — should say reductions of CM point orbits equidistribute. TWO RIGOROUS NEGATIVES I derived/verified for secp256k1 that close the naive versions of 4(d): (1) the Frobenius order Z[pi] has discriminant -3v^2 with v = 303414439467246543595250775667605759171 (128 bits), so |Cl(Z[pi])| ~ 2^128 < n; since n is prime, EVERY group homomorphism Cl(Z[pi]) -> E(F_p) is trivial — there is no class-group transfer, full stop. (2) h(Z[omega]) = 1, so the crater of the isogeny volcano is a single vertex: there is no set of 'maximally CM-structured' isogenous curves to search, and all isogenous curves have the same order n, so none is group-theoretically weaker. The class number being SMALL is an anti-lever, not a lever.
smallest_experiment: PARI/GP only. Pick a toy curve of analytic rank 0 with a rank-1 quadratic twist and small conductor, and a discriminant D satisfying the Heegner hypothesis with h(D) between 4 and 20. Compute the h(D) conjugate Heegner points numerically: for each reduced form [a,b,c] of discriminant D, tau_a = (-b + sqrt(D))/(2a), z(tau) = sum_{n} (a_n/n) q^n with a_n from ellan, then ellztopoint; recognize the orbit algebraically by LLL on the degree-h(D) minimal polynomial of x(P_a); pick a 20-32 bit prime p that splits completely in H_D (factor the min poly mod p and keep a degree-1 root), reduce the whole orbit into E(F_p), brute-force all h(D) discrete logs, then test the function Cl(D) -> Z/n for (i) affine homomorphism, (ii) Fourier support over the abelian group Cl(D), (iii) any linear relation beyond the known trace/Euler-system ones.
kill_criteria: DEAD if the dlog function on Cl(D) is Fourier-flat (max nontrivial coefficient <= C sqrt(h log h)) and admits no linear relations beyond the Euler-system ones, across at least 5 distinct (curve, D) pairs — i.e. the orbit behaves like h(D) independent random points. Also DEAD if the per-point cost of computing the orbit reduction grows faster than poly(h(D)), or if the number of independent relations available among factor-base elements stays O(1) per level while index calculus needs |FB| of them.
expected_complexity: No complexity claim. Best case IF the dlog map were affine over Cl(D): the h(D) factor-base logs come for free from O(1) of them, and combined with a decomposition oracle one would get index calculus at ~|FB|^2; but a decomposition oracle is exactly what is still missing, so even a positive result here is only a necessary, not sufficient, step. What must be true for any win: a computable map from random points of E(F_p) into the CM-orbit span, which currently does not exist.
novelty_note: Every previous lifting attack (xedni, Silverman-Suzuki) foundered on 'not enough height-bounded global points'. Heegner orbits are the one construction that supplies exponentially many such points with poly-size descriptions and a computable group action, so this is the strongest available attack on precisely the gap named in the brief; and the Fourier test on Cl(D) is a decisive, cheap experiment I have not seen run.

title: Does any p-shape-derived subset or low-degree map on E(F_p) have abnormal bias? (with an SNFS-free F_p^* discrete-log oracle lowering the bar)
surface: 4(b)/4(c) — whether the digit structure or fast-reduction structure is visible group-theoretically
hypothesis: Rigidity says there is no nonconstant morphism E -> G_m (a projective variety maps to an affine one only by constants), so no algebraic transfer exists, and pairings are blocked (verified: no embedding degree k <= 2*10^5, gcd(n,p-1)=1) and the formal group is blocked (n != p). What remains is a STATISTICAL transfer. Because p = f(2^32) is SNFS-friendly, a 256-bit discrete log in F_p^* is essentially free, so even a weakly biased map chi: E(F_p) -> F_p^* with chi(P+Q) ~ chi(P)chi(Q) at rate 1/2 + eps, or any digit-defined subset of E(F_p) with a large Fourier coefficient over Z/n, would be an exploitable non-generic lever via hidden-number-problem style lattice attacks.
nongeneric_structure: The base-2^32 digit representation induced by p = f(2^32), the Solinas-style fast-reduction orbit structure, and the SNFS-easiness of the DLP in F_p^* for this specific p. Not a generic search: the statistic being measured is defined by the coordinate representation in F_p, which a generic group oracle hides by definition.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] Boneh-Venkatesan 1996 (hidden number problem / lattice attacks from partial information) — this is what makes a small bias exploitable. [ESTABLISHED] Gordon 1993 for NFS discrete logs in F_p and the SNFS variant with L[1/3, (32/9)^{1/3}] for special p (SEARCH: 'Schirokauer special number field sieve discrete logarithm virtual logarithms' for the exact complexity statement). SEARCH: 'Kohel Shparlinski exponential sums group generators elliptic curves finite fields ANTS 2000' and 'Lange Shparlinski exponential sums elliptic curves random walks' — these should give square-root-cancellation bounds for character sums over x-coordinates of multiples of a point, which PREDICT this idea is dead; the point of measuring is that those bounds are for generic sets/intervals, not for multiplicatively structured digit boxes attached to a special p. [MEASURED HERE] 16-bit pilot (p = 4^8-4-113, n = 64921): digit-box max|Fourier| = 4.06*sqrt(|S|) vs an interval control at 3.93 and a random-set control at 4.21 — already indistinguishable from random.
smallest_experiment: Already prototyped: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-virtualaquarium/e2bf485c-5536-57b5-8ef5-8e69bb3bcc7b/scratchpad/fourier_pilot.py. Extend it: toy primes p = m^8 - m - c with m = 2^3, 2^4, 2^5 (24 to 40 bits) with prime-order y^2 = x^3+7; build the full dlog table (or, past 2^28, a random sample plus Kloosterman-style estimation); for each candidate set S in {digit box, interval, small-norm lifts in O, x in phi(low-degree polynomial values), minimal-3-dim-lattice projective lift statistics, small-norm Eisenstein multiples}, FFT the indicator over Z/n and compare max nontrivial coefficient to sqrt(|S| log n) and to matched random controls. Separately, brute-force search all rational maps chi of degree <= 3 in (x,y) and test multiplicative correlation of chi(P+Q) vs chi(P)chi(Q) over random pairs.
kill_criteria: DEAD if, for every tested family and every toy size up to 40 bits, max nontrivial |Fourier| stays within a factor 1.5 of the matched random control and below C*sqrt(|S| log n), and no degree-<=3 rational map shows multiplicative correlation above the 1/sqrt(sample) noise floor. The 16-bit pilot already fires one of these bullets; two more sizes with the same result ends it.
expected_complexity: No direct complexity claim. If a Fourier coefficient of size delta*|S| were found with delta not tiny, one gets a distinguisher and, via HNP/lattice techniques, plausibly a dlog attack at cost ~ poly/delta^2 — a real break. What must be true: bias substantially above square-root cancellation, which contradicts the expected exponential-sum bounds.
novelty_note: This is the cheapest way to settle 4(c) and half of 4(b) empirically rather than by hand-waving, and it is the only idea here that is already partly executed. Its real value is negative-result value: it closes the 'maybe the fast-reduction/digit structure leaks' family with measurements instead of assertions, and it names the precise reason a weak leak would matter for THIS p (SNFS makes the target group's DLP free).

title: Elliptic surfaces specializing to secp256k1: lattice-built small-coefficient b(t) with b(2^32) = 7 mod p, and Mordell-Weil sections as a graded factor base
surface: 4(a)/4(b)/4(e) — the closest structural analogue of SNFS polynomial selection for an elliptic curve
hypothesis: SNFS polynomial selection picks f with small coefficients and f(m) = 0 mod p. The elliptic analogue: pick b(t) in Z[t] with SMALL coefficients and b(2^32) = 7 mod p, so the elliptic surface y^2 = x^3 + b(t) specializes at t = 2^32 to secp256k1 mod p. That congruence is a single linear condition on the coefficient vector, so LLL yields degree-N families with coefficients of size ~p^{1/(N+1)} (e.g. degree 200 with coefficients below 2^10). If such a b can also be forced to carry many Mordell-Weil sections, the sections give points of E(F_p) with polynomial-size descriptions and a group law (over Q(t)) whose height is the integer DEGREE — a graded structure, which is the closest thing to 'smoothness' available on the elliptic side.
nongeneric_structure: p = f(2^32) turns 'reduces to our curve' into one linear congruence, making the search space of global families enormous and lattice-accessible; plus Shioda's Mordell-Weil lattice theory for y^2 = x^3 + b(t), where section heights are computed from degrees and singular fibre types. Not a generic search: the objects enumerated are polynomial sections of a surface, found by linear algebra over Z, and their images in E(F_p) are a by-product.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] Shioda, 'On the Mordell-Weil lattices', Comment. Math. Univ. St. Pauli 1990 (rank bounded via Shioda-Tate, growing at most linearly in deg b; for deg b <= 6 the MW lattice embeds in E_8 and rank <= 8). [ESTABLISHED] Silverman's specialization theorem (sections specialize injectively for all but finitely many t). [ESTABLISHED] Ulmer 2002 (Annals), 'Elliptic curves with large rank over function fields' — unbounded rank exists in characteristic p function fields, NOT over Q(t); worth checking whether a char-p analogue can be arranged here (SEARCH: 'Ulmer elliptic curves large rank function fields Annals 2002'). Nearest failure mode: this is Silverman-Suzuki lifting again in disguise, and the observation that sections of degree <= 7 specialize EXACTLY into the base-2^32 digit box shows idea 1's factor base is the degree-<=7 part of this construction — a unification I have not seen stated. WHAT IS DIFFERENT: prior lifting attacks fixed a global curve and hunted for points; here the congruence is one linear condition, so the family of admissible global curves is searchable by LLL, and one hunts for surfaces with many sections instead.
smallest_experiment: Toy p = m^8 - m - c (m = 2^5, p ~ 2^40) with prime-order y^2 = x^3+7. Step 1: LLL on the lattice {c in Z^{N+1} : sum c_i m^i = 7 mod p} for N = 6..20 and verify you get b(t) with tiny coefficients and b(m) = 7 mod p (pure linear algebra, minutes). Step 2: for each such b of degree <= 6, enumerate sections by solving Y(t)^2 = X(t)^3 + b(t) with deg X <= 2, deg Y <= 3 via undetermined coefficients plus resultants in PARI; count sections and compute their specializations in E(F_p). Step 3: compare, at equal CPU cost, the number of distinct E(F_p) points obtained from sections against brute-force digit-box enumeration, and test whether section arithmetic over Q(t) gives ANY way to express a random target point (it should not).
kill_criteria: DEAD if (i) every lattice-built b of degree <= 6 has section count at or below the Shioda bound (<= 8) and higher degrees give rank growing only linearly in deg b while |FB| must be p^{1/k}, so sections are always exponentially fewer than brute-force digit points at the same cost; or (ii) no procedure is found that maps a random point of E(F_p) back into the section span better than a knapsack — i.e. the degree grading is destroyed by specialization above degree 7 (coordinates exceed p), which it provably is.
expected_complexity: No win claimed. Best case: if a surface with rank r and an efficient 'reduce a point to a section' algorithm existed (the Cantor-reduction analogue), index calculus would cost ~poly(r) per relation and ~r^2 linear algebra. What must be true: a decomposition algorithm over the section group AND rank growth that outpaces the p^{1/k} factor-base requirement — the Shioda-Tate bound makes the latter linear in degree, which is almost certainly fatal.
novelty_note: It is the only construction here that mirrors SNFS polynomial selection literally (small-height polynomial hitting p), and it explains WHY the digit-box factor base of idea 1 is the right object (degree <= 7 sections) while simultaneously showing where the grading dies (degree 8 and up). Even the negative result is a clean, quantitative statement of why 'SNFS-style polynomial selection' has no elliptic analogue: the relation-rich object in SNFS is a multiplicative monoid with unique factorization, while the elliptic analogue is a Mordell-Weil group whose rank is bounded linearly by geometry.

title: Local Tate duality as a discrete-log functional: ramified n-torsors over Q_p
surface: Surface 5 (lifting to char 0 / p-adic), item (a): making 'lift and measure' work when #E != p
hypothesis: Tate local duality gives a PERFECT pairing between the profinite completion of E(Q_p) and H^1(Q_p,E); since E(Q_p) = Z_p (+) Z/n canonically, a single explicit class c in H^1(Q_p,E)[n] is literally a DL functional, and k = <s(Q),c>/<s(P),c> where s is the canonical torsion section. The hypothesis is that some such class admits a Miller/Weil-reciprocity evaluation in O(log n) operations despite its torsor having index n.
nongeneric_structure: The p-adic field Q_p itself: (i) Hensel lifting plus gcd(n,p)=1 gives the canonical splitting E(Q_p) iso Z_p (+) E(F_p), so every point of E(F_p) has a canonical, efficiently computable characteristic-0 avatar; (ii) the VALUATION makes Q_p*/(Q_p*)^n iso Z/n for any n coprime to p, i.e. Q_p possesses a cyclic quotient of order n even though mu_n is not in Q_p -- F_p has no such quotient (F_p*/(F_p*)^n is trivial when gcd(n,p-1)=1, which is exactly the Frey-Ruck dead end); (iii) the invariant map of the Brauer group of Q_p. This is not a re-encoded generic search: nothing enumerates group elements; the DL is read off as the invariant of a cup product of two explicitly written cohomological objects, evaluated by Weil reciprocity on divisors of a lifted curve.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] Tate, 'WC-groups over p-adic fields', Seminaire Bourbaki 1957/58 (local duality E(K)^ x H^1(K,E) -> Q/Z perfect). [ESTABLISHED] Lichtenbaum, 'The period-index problem for elliptic curves', Amer. J. Math. 1968 (period = index over p-adic fields). [ESTABLISHED] Menezes-Okamoto-Vanstone 1993 and Frey-Ruck 1994 (transfer to mu_n inside F_{q^d}; dead because the embedding degree d is about n for secp256k1). [ESTABLISHED] V. Miller, 'The Weil pairing and its efficient calculation', J. Cryptology 2004 (written 1986): a pairing whose defining function has degree n is nevertheless EVALUATED in O(log n). WHAT IS DIFFERENT: every published transfer attack puts the n-torsion of the target inside a group of roots of unity, forcing the embedding-degree condition. Here the n-torsion of the target comes from the valuation of Q_p and exists unconditionally; the obstruction that replaces embedding degree is period=index (a statement about the SIZE OF A REPRESENTATION, not about a field degree), and Kummer extensions Q_p(p^{1/n}) of degree n do admit O(log n)-size presentations, so the reflex 'degree n therefore cost n' is not automatically valid. SEARCH: 'local Tate duality elliptic curve discrete logarithm ramified torsor' and 'Tate-Lichtenbaum pairing over p-adic field good reduction triviality' -- the result should say that for good reduction and p not dividing n, E(K)/nE(K) is the exact annihilator of the UNRAMIFIED part of H^1(K,E[n]), which is the precise reason the naive Miller computation over Q_p returns an n-th power.
smallest_experiment: PARI/GP on the verified toy curves y^2=x^3+7 with prime order (p=1048783,n=1050337; p=16777723,n=16773667; p=4294968199,n=4295016211) generated by /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-virtualaquarium/e2bf485c-5536-57b5-8ef5-8e69bb3bcc7b/scratchpad/toy7.gp. Step 1: build the canonical torsion section s(P) = m*Ptilde with m = 1 mod n and m = 0 mod p^k, and verify numerically that it is independent of the lift (my /tmp/.../scratchpad/padic2.gp already shows the CONTRASTING naive measurement, log(n*Ptilde)/p mod p, moves affinely with the lift parameter c and sweeps all of F_p -- zero information). Step 2: run Miller's algorithm over Q_p (t_PADIC arithmetic) to compute f_{n,s(P)}(D_{s(Q)}) in Q_p*/(Q_p*)^n and test whether the value is an n-th power (test = valuation divisible by n AND unit part an n-th power in Z_p*). Step 3: validate the implementation on toy curves deliberately chosen with gcd(n,p-1)=m>1, where a nonzero value MUST appear; confirm it reproduces the finite-field Frey-Ruck pairing. Step 4: the real test -- repeat step 2 over compactly represented ramified Kummer extensions L = Q_p[pi]/(pi^d - p) for d = 2..64, where unramified orthogonality does not apply, and measure both nontriviality and the number of nonzero coefficients needed to represent the intermediate Miller values.
kill_criteria: DEAD if, over 100+ toy curves with gcd(n,p-1)=1, the Miller value over Q_p is an n-th power in every case (pairing identically trivial), AND in step 4 the intermediate Miller values over Q_p[pi]/(pi^d-p) require Theta(d) nonzero coefficients (so the cost of the ramified computation scales linearly in the degree, hence linearly in n when d=n is needed). Also DEAD if step 3 shows the only nonzero component is exactly the finite-field Frey-Ruck pairing, i.e. the p-adic setting contributes no information beyond embedding degree.
expected_complexity: poly(log n) group/field operations IF (i) some class c in H^1(Q_p,E)[n] is split by an extension with an O(log n)-size presentation (Kummer extensions are the only plausible candidate), (ii) the cup product with c is computable by Weil reciprocity with O(log n) field operations in that presentation, and (iii) the resulting functional is nonzero on the Z/n summand of E(Q_p). My own theoretical expectation is that good reduction forces (iii) to fail over Q_p itself (E(Q_p)/n sits in the unramified part, which is the exact annihilator of the unramified classes), so the whole idea rests on whether ramified base change can be made sparse.
novelty_note: This is NOT 'MOV/Frey-Ruck restated'. Those attacks fail because mu_n lives only in F_{q^d} with d of size n. The target here, Q_p*/(Q_p*)^n iso Z/n, has n-torsion for free from the valuation, with no embedding-degree condition at all; the replacement obstruction is period=index, which is about representation size. It is also not the anomalous-curve attack: that attack maps into a PRO-p group and therefore annihilates the prime-to-p part of E(F_p) identically (this is the exact reason it yields zero bits for secp256k1, and it is why no variant of 'lift to Z/p^2 and measure the obstruction' can ever work -- the sequence 0 -> F_p -> E(Z/p^2) -> E(F_p) -> 0 splits CANONICALLY because gcd(n,p)=1, via the lift-independent section m*Ptilde with m = 1 mod n, m = 0 mod p; I verified the complementary statement numerically). The present idea is the only way I can see to get a target group that actually contains n-torsion without paying the embedding degree.

title: Elliptic-unit smoothness: a factor base from the canonical CM torsion lift
surface: Surface 5, item (b): height/CM-controlled lifts, pushed to the canonical (torsion) lift
hypothesis: Because E has CM by Z[omega] with h(-3)=1 and Frobenius pi, E(F_p) is canonically iso to O_K/(pi-1) and every point is the reduction of an explicit (pi-1)-torsion point of the j=0 CM curve over the ray class field K_{(pi-1)}. If norms of differences x(Ptilde)-x(Qtilde) factor over small primes (the Gross-Zagier singular-moduli phenomenon), smooth values give a factor base and index calculus becomes possible.
nongeneric_structure: CM by Z[omega], D=-3, j=0: explicit class field theory over K=Q(sqrt(-3)) with class number 1, Shimura reciprocity identifying Gal(K_f/K) with (O_K/f)*, and the theory of elliptic units (values of Weierstrass/Siegel functions at torsion points) whose prime factorizations are computed by Kronecker's second limit formula. The relation-detection step is INTEGER FACTORIZATION of a global norm -- an operation with no meaning whatsoever on opaque group encodings, so this is not a disguised generic search.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] Gross & Zagier, 'On singular moduli', J. reine angew. Math. 1985 (differences of singular moduli factor into small primes with an exact formula). [ESTABLISHED] Kubert & Lang, 'Modular Units' (1981); Coates & Wiles 1977 for elliptic units in the CM setting. SEARCH: 'Robert unites elliptiques 1973' -- should give the construction of elliptic units of a given conductor for an imaginary quadratic field. [ESTABLISHED] Silverman & Suzuki, 'Elliptic curve discrete logarithms and the index calculus', ASIACRYPT 1998, and V. Miller, CRYPTO 1985: lifting points to a global curve to build a factor base fails for height reasons. WHAT IS DIFFERENT: prior lifting index calculus lifts a point to a NON-CANONICAL global point of a rank-r curve and hopes its coordinates are smooth (they essentially never exist at all). Here the lift is canonical and always exists (the torsion section), and the smoothness question concerns an object with a closed-form factorization theory rather than a pseudo-random integer. EXACT QUANTITATIVE OBSTRUCTION I already expect: for prime conductor (pi-1) of norm n, the relevant algebraic numbers are UNITS, so their valuations are supported only at primes dividing the conductor and the factor base is empty; additionally h(-3)=1 collapses the isogeny-volcano/class-group structure that makes CM index calculus work for isogeny problems. The only escape is an auxiliary composite conductor (pi-1)*m with m small, so that Robert units acquire valuations at primes above m.
smallest_experiment: On p=1048783,n=1050337 and p=16777723,n=16773667 (b=7, prime order): compute pi via Cornacchia (4p = a^2+3b^2), check O_K/(pi-1) iso Z/n. For random k, form P and Q=kP in E(F_p). Rather than constructing the degree-~n ray class field, compute the NORM down to K directly as a resultant of division polynomials over Z using PARI polresultant (norms of differences of torsion coordinates are resultants of the relevant division polynomials), then factor with factorint. Record, over 10^4 values of k, (i) whether the norm is a unit / supported only on primes dividing n, (ii) the smooth part with respect to a bound B=10^5, (iii) the mutual information between the factorization pattern and k. Repeat with auxiliary conductor multiplied by small m (m = 2,3,5,7) to test the escape route.
kill_criteria: DEAD if, over 10^4 samples, every norm is +-1 or supported exactly on the primes dividing n (as elliptic-unit theory predicts), OR if the smooth part is statistically independent of k (mutual information below the 10^4-sample noise floor, about 0.01 bits), OR if the auxiliary-conductor variant produces valuations that depend only on k mod m (i.e. it merely recovers Pohlig-Hellman information modulo the auxiliary modulus, which is useless since n is prime).
expected_complexity: L_n(1/2) or better IF (i) the norms behave like random integers of their size with respect to smoothness, (ii) multiplicative relations among smooth values translate into ADDITIVE relations among the corresponding points, and (iii) the relation matrix can be assembled without already knowing any discrete logarithm. I consider (i) very unlikely to hold precisely because the theory says these numbers are units.
novelty_note: The standard 'CM does not help' statement is about point counting and about the GLV endomorphism speedup. What is being tested here is a sharper and rarely stated question: the canonical torsion lift makes the ECDLP EQUIVALENT to an explicit class field theory problem (identify which of the n primes above p in the ray class field of conductor (pi-1) is the one inducing the given reduction), and index calculus in the multiplicative analogue works only because Z has small elements with nontrivial factorizations. The experiment measures directly whether the elliptic analogue has any non-unit global objects at all. A negative result is itself a clean, quantitative closure of the entire 'CM + lifting' route rather than a vague appeal to heights.

title: Covering exponent of a fixed high-rank j=0 Mordell-Weil lattice, with rational-reconstruction recognizability
surface: Surface 5, item (b): height control and low-height lifts, quantified
hypothesis: A lifting index calculus needs a random point of E(F_p) to be the reduction of a global point of RECOGNIZABLE height with non-negligible probability. Recognizability is free: a global x = a/b with |a|,|b| <= sqrt(p) is detected from x mod p by 2-dimensional lattice reduction in O(log p) time. The hypothesis is that the covering probability, boosted by the CM/Z[omega] structure of the Mordell-Weil lattice of y^2=x^3+b over Q(omega), decays slower than the naive (log H)^{r/2} count.
nongeneric_structure: Two things a generic group cannot see: (1) the coordinate representation in F_p -- rational reconstruction of x mod p is an efficiently decidable, discrete-log-free membership test for the factor base; (2) the Neron-Tate canonical height, a genuinely NON-HOMOMORPHIC (quadratic) invariant, which is the only kind of invariant capable of beating the generic bound, since every homomorphic lift-based construction factors through the canonical splitting and yields zero bits. The special shape p = 2^256 - 2^32 - 977 offers a variant recognizability test (SNFS-style base-2^32 representatives in a degree-8 field), which is the same 2-dimensional idea in dimension 8.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] V. Miller, CRYPTO 1985, remarks that lifting points to Q does not produce relations. [ESTABLISHED] Silverman & Suzuki, ASIACRYPT 1998, 'Elliptic curve discrete logarithms and the index calculus': the height/rank obstruction to lifting-based index calculus. [ESTABLISHED] Silverman, 'The xedni calculus and the elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem', Designs Codes Cryptogr. 1999/2000. [ESTABLISHED] Jacobson, Koblitz, Silverman, Stein, Teske, 'Analysis of the xedni calculus attack', Designs Codes Cryptogr. 2000. SEARCH: 'Elkies rank 28 elliptic curve 2006 NMBRTHRY' and 'Elkies Klagsbrun rank 29 elliptic curve 2020' -- should confirm the record Mordell-Weil ranks over Q. SEARCH: 'Elkies Mordell curve high rank y^2 = x^3 + k rank 17' -- should confirm the record rank within the j=0 family is far below the general record. WHAT IS DIFFERENT FROM XEDNI: xedni picks a NEW curve per relation and needs a rank DROP (probability essentially zero). Here one fixed curve of maximal rank is used and the only question is the covering exponent of its Mordell-Weil lattice, plus the CM bonus from lambda acting on the lattice (which halves the number of generators that must be found and gives a hexagonal-packing density bonus).
smallest_experiment: Verified inputs: PARI ellanalyticrank over b=1..40 gives ranks 0-2, with b=15,17,24,37 of rank 2 (script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-virtualaquarium/e2bf485c-5536-57b5-8ef5-8e69bb3bcc7b/scratchpad/rank.gp). Pick b with rank r=1,2,3 (search b up to 10^4 for rank 3-4). For toy primes of 20, 24 and 32 bits with y^2=x^3+b of prime order (regenerate with the toy.gp search, changing b), obtain Mordell-Weil generators via PARI ellgenerators/ellheegner, enumerate ALL global points with canonical height <= H by lattice enumeration in the generator basis for H = 5,10,20,40,80, reduce each mod p, and measure the covering fraction C(H) = (number of distinct reductions)/n. Fit C(H) = c * H^e / n and compare the fitted e to r/2. Then include the lambda-orbit (points over Q(omega), obtained by applying the CM endomorphism to the reductions) and measure the multiplicative bonus constant. Finally, measure directly how many of the n points of E(F_p) admit ANY rational reconstruction x = a/b, |a|,|b| <= sqrt(p), that actually lies on the global curve.
kill_criteria: DEAD if the fitted exponent e equals r/2 within +-0.1 and the CM bonus constant is at most (2/sqrt(3))^{r/2}(1+o(1)). Under that fit, the 256-bit requirement (count of points of height <= H must reach n = 2^256, with H <= (1/2)log p which is about 89 in natural log, and lattice minimum at best about 1) forces Z-rank r >= 65 to 95, versus the record 28-29 over Q and far less within the j=0 family. Also DEAD if the direct rational-reconstruction count finds 0 usable lifts at 32 bits, since the count can only get worse as p grows.
expected_complexity: Relation collection in poly time IF (i) curves of rank >= 65 with explicitly known generators existed (nothing remotely close is known) and (ii) the reduction map could be inverted on a given target. Crucial honesty point: inverting the reduction map using only FORWARD evaluations is itself a generic search (it is a modular knapsack with weights one can evaluate but not read), so a genuine win additionally requires a height-based, non-homomorphic inversion -- which is exactly what the recognizability test is meant to provide and exactly what the experiment measures.
novelty_note: This is not a restatement of 'lifting fails by heights' -- it converts that slogan into a single measurable number (the covering exponent e) and a single explicit threshold (required rank about 65-95), and it separately isolates the CM contribution, answering the prompt's question (does CM raise the chance of a low-height lift?) quantitatively: the answer is that CM changes only the packing CONSTANT, roughly (2/sqrt(3))^{r/2}, which lowers the required rank by about 4 percent and therefore cannot matter. It also makes explicit the usually-unstated point that recognizability of a lift (rational reconstruction) is the actual non-generic resource, not the lift itself.

title: Xedni with a degree-d coefficient field: escaping the 9-point cap and scaling Mestre-in-reverse
surface: Surface 5, item (d): Mestre-style rank manipulation, with the coefficient field degree as the new variable
hypothesis: Xedni is capped at r <= 9 lifted points because a plane cubic over Q has 10 coefficients. Over a degree-d number field there are 10d rational parameters, so about 9d points can be forced while simultaneously imposing roughly d times as many local (Mestre-in-reverse) rank-lowering conditions. If the achievable rank deficit grows linearly in d while the number of forced points also grows linearly in d, the per-trial success probability might stop collapsing.
nongeneric_structure: Mordell-Weil rank theory and canonical heights over number fields, root numbers and local conditions at small primes (Mestre's method), and the CM base field Q(omega) matched to the j=0 structure of the target. Nothing here is a group-operation search: the attack succeeds or fails on an arithmetic property (the rank of a specific global curve) that is invisible in the generic model.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] Silverman, 'The xedni calculus and the elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem', Designs Codes Cryptogr. 1999/2000 (including the use of Mestre's method in reverse to lower the rank of the lifted curve). [ESTABLISHED] Jacobson, Koblitz, Silverman, Stein, Teske, 'Analysis of the xedni calculus attack', Designs Codes Cryptogr. 2000: the lifted points are independent with probability essentially 1 and the attack is no better than exhaustive search. SEARCH: 'Mestre methode construction courbes elliptiques rang eleve 1991' -- should confirm the local-conditions heuristic for raising rank. WHAT IS DIFFERENT: the JKSTW analysis is entirely at d=1. The single variable changed here is the coefficient field degree, which scales BOTH the number of points that can be forced onto the cubic AND the number of imposable local conditions; no published analysis measures whether the rank deficit achievable by Mestre-in-reverse grows with d or stays O(1).
smallest_experiment: Implement the xedni construction over K = Q(omega) (matching the CM setting) at 20-24 bits using the verified toy curves (p=1048783,n=1050337; p=16777723,n=16773667). For r = 4..8 forced points, solve the linear system for the cubic's coefficients in O_K, then estimate the rank of the resulting curve. Tooling note measured in this session: PARI's ellrank works over Q only in this build, so for the base-changed curve use rank(E/K) = rank(E/Q) + rank(E^{(-3)}/Q) via the quadratic twist decomposition, both computable with PARI ellrank/ellanalyticrank -- this keeps the whole experiment in PARI-GP. Measure the empirical Pr[rank < r] as a function of (r, number of imposed local conditions) and of log p by rerunning at 20 and 24 bits, and fit the decay exponent.
kill_criteria: DEAD if log(1/Pr[rank < r]) grows at least linearly in log p with slope >= 1/2 for every tested d (that matches or beats rho's own exponent, so the attack cannot win), OR if imposing Mestre-in-reverse conditions over Q(omega) shifts the mean rank of the lifted curve by only O(1) rather than Theta(d) -- which would confirm that extra parameters buy forced points but not rank deficit.
expected_complexity: Sub-exponential only if the achievable rank deficit grows proportionally to the number of forced points. That would require the local conditions at small primes to lower the rank by Theta(d), contradicting the standard heuristic that each forced point contributes an independent unit of rank; I know of no mechanism that would make it true.
novelty_note: Proposed only because the prompt explicitly allows a known dead end with a named difference: the difference is the coefficient field degree d, the one parameter the published xedni analysis holds fixed at 1, and the experiment produces a scaling law in d rather than an anecdote. The quadratic-twist trick makes the rank estimation runnable in PARI alone, which is why this is testable at all without Magma or Sage.

title: Elliptic divisibility sequences: CRT over ranks of apparition instead of one p-adic lift
surface: Surface 5, item (c): several lifts combined by CRT / p-adic approximation
hypothesis: For a global point R on E/Q with elliptic divisibility sequence W, a prime l divides W_m exactly when the rank of apparition rho_l divides m, and ord_p(W_{k rho}) = ord_p(W_rho) + ord_p(k). If the discrete log k could be recovered as k mod rho_l for many auxiliary primes l at O(log) cost each, CRT reconstructs k once the product of the rho_l exceeds n -- a genuine multi-place attack rather than a single p-adic measurement.
nongeneric_structure: Elliptic divisibility sequences are characteristic-0 INTEGER sequences obeying the Ward/Somos recursion; their divisibility structure and the valuation law are arithmetic facts about global objects, not about the abstract group. Divisibility of an integer term by an auxiliary prime l is meaningless for an opaque encoding, so the proposal is not a re-encoded generic search -- it is an attempt to read the same index k at many independent places.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] M. Ward, 'Memoir on elliptic divisibility sequences', Amer. J. Math. 1948 (rank of apparition and the divisibility structure). SEARCH: 'Shipsey elliptic divisibility sequences thesis 2001 Goldsmiths' -- should give the O(log m) algorithm for computing W_m mod p by a doubling chain. SEARCH: 'Lauter Stange elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem equivalent hard problems elliptic divisibility sequences SAC 2008' -- should state an EQUIVALENCE between ECDLP and EDS residue/association problems. WHAT IS DIFFERENT: the known results are equivalences (they show the EDS formulation is no easier), not an analysis of the multi-prime CRT variant, which no equivalence result forbids on its own. THE EXACT OBSTRUCTION TO BEAT, stated quantitatively: (i) the valuation law ord_p(W_{k rho}) = ord_p(W_rho) + ord_p(k) only ever exposes the p-PART of the index, which is trivial because gcd(n,p)=1 -- this is precisely the same annihilation that makes the Smart/Satoh-Araki/Semaev anomalous attack yield zero bits here; and (ii) the CRT components live in the global integer W_k, whose size obeys log|W_k| approximately h(R) k^2, so at k about 2^256 the object carrying the information has on the order of 2^512 bits.
smallest_experiment: On the 24- and 32-bit toy curves (p=16777723,n=16773667; p=4294968199,n=4295016211): pick a positive-rank Mordell curve y^2=x^3+b with a known generator R (b=2,3,5,8 all have analytic rank 1, measured in this session). Compute the exact integer EDS W_m for m <= 10^4 in Python with gmpy2, and in parallel W_m mod p by Shipsey's doubling chain. Then measure: (1) the empirical mutual information between (W_m mod p) and the vector (ord_l(W_m)) for all l <= 10^5, over 10^5 sampled m; (2) the convergence of log|W_m|/m^2 to the canonical height h(R), to confirm the size barrier; (3) whether any rho_l is computable from mod-p data alone, by checking whether the map m -> (W_m mod p) determines l | W_m at rates above chance.
kill_criteria: DEAD if the mutual information in (1) is at or below the 10^5-sample noise floor (about 0.005 bits) for every l <= 10^5, AND log|W_m|/m^2 converges to h(R) (confirming that the object holding the CRT information has about 2^512 bits at cryptographic size). Either of these alone is decisive; both together close the multi-place route.
expected_complexity: Polynomial IF k mod rho_l were computable in poly time per auxiliary prime l and the product of the rho_l exceeded n. What must be true for that: a cheap 'CRT transfer' carrying mod-p data of a global object to its mod-l data -- which is exactly what the independence of residues at distinct places forbids. I state this as the reason I expect failure, not as a hope.
novelty_note: The value is that it converts the vague suggestion 'use several lifts and CRT' into a single measurable quantity (mutual information between mod-p sequence data and auxiliary-prime valuations) and into one sharp size law (log|W_k| about h(R)k^2, hence 2^512 bits). It also makes explicit that the anomalous-curve attack and the EDS valuation law are the SAME phenomenon -- the formal-group filtration -- which is why both see only the p-part of the index and both return exactly zero bits when gcd(n,p)=1, as I confirmed numerically for the p-adic side.

title: The (p/B)^g decomposition wall for covers over prime fields, and the only escape hatch (mu6-symmetric summation polynomials on the cover)
surface: 6 — transfer maps: covers/correspondences into higher-genus Jacobians over F_p
hypothesis: Any degree-d cover C -> E over the PRIME field F_p lands E(F_p) inside Jac(C)(F_p) of size ~p^g, and generic relation search there costs >= p, so the only conceivable win is a decomposition oracle that is not probabilistic-fiber-hitting; the j=0 mu6 automorphism group acting on C could cut the Groebner degree of the cover's summation/decomposition system enough to make that oracle cheap.
nongeneric_structure: Coordinate/field structure of F_p (factor bases are sets of x-coordinates, decomposition is polynomial system solving) plus Aut(E)=mu6 for j=0, which lifts to an automorphism group of any mu3- or mu6-equivariant cover and acts on the decomposition system, permitting symmetrization of the summation polynomials. Not a re-encoded generic search: relations are found by solving multivariate polynomial systems over F_p, which the generic group model forbids.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] Gaudry 2000 'An algorithm for solving the discrete log problem on hyperelliptic curves' (O(q^2) for fixed genus); Gaudry-Theriault-Thome-Diem ~2007 'A double large prime variation for small genus hyperelliptic index calculus' (~q^(2-2/g)); Enge-Gaudry 2002 subexponential L(1/2) only when g/log q -> infinity; Gaudry-Hess-Smart 2002 GHS Weil descent (needs composite-degree extensions, inapplicable to prime p); Semaev 2004 summation polynomials; Diem 2011 'On the discrete logarithm problem in elliptic curves' (subexponential only over F_q^n with n growing); Faugere-Gaudry-Huot-Renault ~2014 'Using symmetries in the index calculus for elliptic curves DLP'. Why they failed here: all small-genus index calculus needs the base field to SHRINK (q = n^(1/g)), impossible for prime n ~ p. What is DIFFERENT: I am not proposing the fiber-hitting relation search at all; I am proposing to use the cover only as a carrier for a mu6-symmetrized decomposition system and to measure the actual Groebner degree, which is the single unmeasured quantity in the chain. SEARCH: 'summation polynomials j-invariant 0 symmetry Groebner degree prime field' — result should say whether anyone has measured the degree of regularity for mu3/mu6-symmetrized systems over prime fields.
smallest_experiment: On 20-32 bit curves y^2=x^3+7 over p=1 mod 3 with prime order: (1) build the mu3 cover C: y^2 = z^9 + 7 (x = z^3) and the bielliptic genus-2 covers obtained from degree-2 maps; (2) implement Gaudry-style index calculus in Jac(C)(F_p) with factor base = {points with z in a subset S of size B}, and MEASURE the empirical number of group operations per relation as a function of B/p, checking the predicted (p/B)^g law; (3) separately, write the 3rd/4th summation polynomial of E, symmetrize it under the substitution x -> beta*x, and measure the Groebner degree of regularity (msolve or Singular, or a small F4 in Python; PARI-GP for the curve arithmetic) as p grows over 20,24,28,32 bits.
kill_criteria: DEAD if (a) the measured relation cost follows (p/B)^g within a constant factor for g=2,3 (confirming no cheap oracle), AND (b) the degree of regularity of the mu6-symmetrized summation system grows with log p (rather than staying bounded), so that extrapolated relation cost at 256 bits exceeds 2^128. Also DEAD immediately if the symmetrization reduces the number of monomials by less than the trivial factor 6.
expected_complexity: Best case p^(1/2-eps) only if a mu6-symmetrized decomposition oracle runs in time polynomial in log p for factor bases of size <= p^(1/2); otherwise the honest floor is Omega(p) (i.e. 2^256 for secp256k1), since with factor base size B and genus g the expected cost per relation is ~(p/B)^g >= p^(g/2) >= p for g>=2, B<=p^(1/2).
novelty_note: The textbook dead end is 'GHS/cover attacks need extension fields'. I am not re-running GHS; I am isolating the exact quantity (degree of regularity of a mu6-symmetrized decomposition system over a prime field) that is the only free parameter left, and the experiment produces a number nobody quotes for j=0. Even a negative result yields the sharp statement: cover attacks over prime fields are bounded below by p, the SQUARE of the rho bound.

title: Elliptic Gauss sums: cubic/sextic residue characters of x-coordinates as a lambda-equivariant transfer out of the group
surface: 6 — transfer maps: (a) maps that are not group homomorphisms but preserve enough structure
hypothesis: The cubic residue character chi_3(x(R)) is genuinely lambda-equivariant (chi_3(x(lambda R)) = chi_3(beta) chi_3(x(R))), so the pair (x-coordinate, cubic character) carries CM-compatible structure absent for generic curves; if the associated twisted point counts (Frobenius traces on the mu3/mu6 covers of E) can be made to depend on the specific point Q = kP rather than only on E, the discrete log would be recoverable from bounded-genus character sums.
nongeneric_structure: The field structure of F_p (cubic residue symbol, p = 1 mod 3) coupled to j=0: the endomorphism acts on x-coordinates by the LINEAR map x -> beta*x, and beta is a non-cube, so the multiplicative character sees the endomorphism. Verified numerically on a 20-bit toy curve. This is not a generic search because it reads the residue symbol of a coordinate, an operation the generic group model does not provide.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] classical Eisenstein/Jacobi-sum theory: for y^2=x^3+D over F_p with p=1 mod 3, #E(F_p) is given by a Jacobi sum / the representation 4p = L^2 + 27M^2 (Gauss); Ireland-Rosen, 'A Classical Introduction to Modern Number Theory', ch. 11, has the cubic-character point count. [ESTABLISHED] Kohel-Shparlinski and others proved uniform distribution / character-sum bounds for x(kP) over subgroups, which is evidence AGAINST leakage. SEARCH: 'elliptic Gauss sums Shipsey Stange character sums coordinates discrete logarithm' and 'Kohel Shparlinski exponential sums elliptic curve discrete logarithm distribution' — results should say that character sums over {kP} are square-root cancelling, i.e. no exploitable bias.
smallest_experiment: Already partly run: on p=413713, n=413299, chi_3(x(kP)) is equidistributed and shows <=2.7 sigma deviation against k mod 2,3,4,5,7,9. Next step (hours): for 24-32 bit curves, compute the full vector (chi_6(x(kP)), chi_2(y(kP))) and run a Fourier/Walsh test for ANY non-trivial additive character psi of Z/n with a Fourier coefficient above the sqrt(n) noise floor, i.e. test |sum_k chi(x(kP)) e(ak/n)| >> sqrt(n) for some a. Also compute the Frobenius traces of the twisted covers y^2 = z^9 + 7 and compare across different base points P to confirm they are P-independent.
kill_criteria: DEAD if for all 24-32 bit curves the maximum Fourier coefficient of chi(x(kP)) over all non-trivial a stays within a small constant of sqrt(n) (Weil square-root cancellation), and if the cover trace vector is provably identical for all choices of P (which it is, since the cover depends only on E). The second condition alone is near-fatal and is the first thing to check.
expected_complexity: No complexity claim. At best this yields log_2(6) bits of free classification for rho (already subsumed by the known automorphism speedup). A win would require a Fourier coefficient of size n^(1/2+delta), which would contradict Weil-type bounds.
novelty_note: The textbook dead end is 'MOV/Frey-Ruck need small embedding degree'. This is a different transfer: out of the group into mu_3 via a residue symbol, not into F_p^k*. The specific lambda-equivariance relation chi(x(lambda R)) = chi(beta) chi(x(R)) is a real, verified, CM-specific identity, and the experiment is cheap enough that confirming the negative closes a family of 'use the residue symbol' ideas permanently.

title: A point-to-class-group map: the sqrt(p)-sized budget that makes even a partial map devastating
surface: 6 — transfer maps: (a) a map to a class group, which has subexponential DLP
hypothesis: If there is ANY efficiently computable map Psi: E(F_p) -> Cl(O) (O an imaginary quadratic order of discriminant ~ -p, so #Cl(O) ~ sqrt(p)) that is a homomorphism on a noticeable subset, then Hafner-McCurley subexponential class-group DL recovers ~half the bits of k and leaves only ~2^64 work for secp256k1; so it is worth an exhaustive small-scale search for such a Psi among CM-natural candidates.
nongeneric_structure: The CM structure: End(E) = Z[omega] is the maximal order of Q(sqrt(-3)) with class number 1, Frobenius pi in Z[omega] with N(pi)=p, and E(F_p) is isomorphic to Z[omega]/(pi-1) as a Z[omega]-module with lambda acting as omega. Class groups of orders Z + f*Z[omega] (f ~ sqrt(p) the conductor of Z[pi]) are the only nearby groups with subexponential DLP. This is not a generic re-encoding because Psi must read the coordinates of the point, e.g. via binary quadratic forms built from x(R) mod small primes.
prior_work:
[ESTABLISHED] Hafner-McCurley 1989, subexponential L(1/2) class group computation; Deuring correspondence / Waterhouse: isogeny classes of ordinary curves correspond to Cl(O) torsors, so the SET of curves is a Cl(O)-torsor of size h(O) ~ sqrt(p). Why the obvious route fails: isogenies and kernel ideals see only the SUBGROUP generated by a point, and since n is prime =

for every Q, so any construction factoring through is constant in k. [SPECULATION] whether a coordinate-level map exists at all. SEARCH: 'map from points of an elliptic curve to the ideal class group of the endomorphism ring' — expected result: no such map is known, and the natural candidates are constant.
smallest_experiment: On 20-24 bit toy curves with SMALL class number (choose p so that disc(Z[pi]) = t^2-4p = -3 f^2 with f having a small class-number order): enumerate all points R = kP, and evaluate a parameterized family of candidate maps -- (i) R -> class of the form [ell, x(R) mod ell, *] for small split primes ell, (ii) R -> class of the ideal generated by (x(R) lifted to Z, sqrt(-3)), (iii) R -> product over small ell of Legendre-symbol-selected classes -- and test each for (a) non-constancy and (b) the homomorphism property Psi(R+S) = Psi(R)Psi(S) on random triples. PARI-GP has qfbred/qfbcompos and bnfinit for the class group arithmetic.
kill_criteria: DEAD if every candidate Psi in the family is either constant, or fails Psi(R+S)=Psi(R)Psi(S) on more than a 1/h fraction of random triples (i.e. behaves like a random function), for all toy curves tested. A structural kill also applies if one proves any Galois-equivariant map E(F_p) -> Cl(O) must factor through the subgroup generated, hence be constant.
expected_complexity: If a homomorphic Psi with image of size ~sqrt(p) existed: L_p(1/2) for the class group DL plus p^(1/4) for the residual search, i.e. ~2^64 for secp256k1. This requires Psi to be a genuine group homomorphism on a set of density 1/polylog, which is what the experiment tests.
novelty_note: Usually dismissed with 'class groups are unrelated to E(F_p)'. The contribution is the explicit budget: because h(O) ~ sqrt(p), a map that is only HALF informative already breaks secp256k1, which sets a much lower bar than people assume and justifies an exhaustive search over natural candidates rather than a hand-wave.

title: Two-dimensional elliptic nets over Z[omega]: inverting a bilinear recurrence instead of searching a group
surface: 6 — transfer maps: transfer to a linear/bilinear recurrence object rather than to another group
hypothesis: The sequence m -> x(mP) is not an arbitrary function: it is generated by the Somos-4 / elliptic divisibility sequence recurrence, and the CM structure upgrades it to a Z[omega]-indexed elliptic NET W(u,v) attached to the pair (P, lambda P) with the answer sitting at a lattice point (u,v) of size ~sqrt(n); the extra relations of the 2D net may make index-recovery an algebraically solvable system rather than a search.
nongeneric_structure: The division-polynomial/EDS bilinear recurrence W(m+k)W(m-k) = W(m+1)W(m-1)W(k)^2 - W(k+1)W(k-1)W(m)^2 is an algebraic identity on coordinates in F_p, invisible in the generic group model; the CM by Z[omega] means the net is indexed by a rank-2 lattice with the GLV decomposition k = u + v*ell, |u|,|v| ~ sqrt(n), giving two independent recurrence directions plus the compatibility relations between them.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] Rachel Shipsey 2001 PhD thesis 'Elliptic divisibility sequences' (EDS-based ECDLP algorithms); Katherine Stange 2007/2008 'The Tate pairing via elliptic nets' (elliptic nets, Z^n-indexed); Lauter and Stange, SAC 2008, 'The elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem and equivalent hard problems for elliptic divisibility sequences' — shows EDS-Association is equivalent to ECDLP in general, with special cases solvable. Why they failed: the 1D EDS index-recovery is exactly as hard as ECDLP. What is DIFFERENT: the 2D (Z[omega]-indexed) net has more relations per unknown than the 1D EDS, and the unknown coordinates are sqrt(n)-sized rather than n-sized, so the natural algebraic system is smaller; nobody, as far as I can tell, has measured the Groebner behaviour of the 2D net inversion. SEARCH: 'elliptic net rank 2 index recovery Groebner discrete logarithm' — expected result: pairing computation only, not inversion.
smallest_experiment: On 20-26 bit curves: compute ell (the lambda eigenvalue), take P and Q=kP for known k, decompose k = u + v*ell with |u|,|v| ~ sqrt(n) by lattice reduction, build the 2D net values W(u,v) from the double-and-add net recurrence (Stange's algorithm, ~100 lines of Python), and set up the polynomial system whose unknowns are the bits/digits of (u,v) truncated to the top j digits. Measure how the Groebner solving time and degree of regularity scale as a function of j and of log p (msolve or Singular). Compare against plain BSGS with the same partial information.
kill_criteria: DEAD if the degree of regularity of the net-inversion system grows linearly (or worse) in the number of unknown digits, so that solving is never better than sqrt of the remaining search space; equivalently, DEAD if the measured time to recover (u,v) exceeds c * sqrt(n) for 20,22,24,26 bits with a growing constant c. Also DEAD if the 2D net relations are shown to be algebraically dependent on the 1D ones (no new information).
expected_complexity: Best case n^(1/4+eps) (solve for u and v separately with algebraic relations replacing one of the two sqrt(n) searches), which requires the net inversion system in one variable of size sqrt(n) to be solvable in subexponential time in log n. No evidence this holds; the honest default is that it is equivalent to ECDLP, per Lauter-Stange.
novelty_note: Not the textbook 'EDS attack' (which is 1D and provably equivalent to ECDLP): the specific new object is the rank-2 net indexed by Z[omega] that exists only because of the j=0 CM, and the measured quantity is the degree of regularity of its inversion system, which is not in the literature.

title: Artificial descent to Z/p^k, Z/pq and Z[omega]/pi^k: the gcd(n,p)=1 splitting wall and the one non-homomorphic loophole
surface: 6 — transfer maps: (b) embedding E(F_p) into a group over an auxiliary ring
hypothesis: Every ring-descent variant (E over Z/p^2, Z/p^k, Z/pq, Z[omega]/pi^k) dies for the same reason -- gcd(n,p)=1 forces a CANONICAL splitting E(Z/p^k) = E(Z/p^k)[n] x E_1, so the lift carries no information about k -- and the only surviving loophole is a NON-homomorphic statistical leak in the higher p-adic digits of the canonical n-torsion lift; this should be measured once and for all.
nongeneric_structure: Lifting to characteristic 0 / to Z_p: the formal group, the p-adic elliptic logarithm, and the fact that beta lifts by Hensel to a cube root of unity in Z_p so that E/Z_p retains CM by Z[omega] and lambda acts on the formal group by multiplication by beta-tilde. This is concretely non-generic because it manipulates coordinates in Z/p^k, not opaque encodings.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] Smart 1999 'The discrete logarithm problem on elliptic curves of trace one', also Satoh-Araki 1998 and Semaev 1998: the p-adic elliptic log breaks ANOMALOUS curves (n=p) precisely because multiplication by n=p pushes the lift ambiguity from E_1 into E_2. For n != p, n is a unit in Z_p, the ambiguity survives, and the sequence 0 -> E_1 -> E(Z_p) -> E(F_p) -> 0 splits canonically. [ESTABLISHED] E(Z/pq) = E(F_p) x E(F_q) by CRT, so the auxiliary prime q contributes nothing about k. Different here: I add the lambda-equivariance question (does requiring the lift to be lambda-equivariant pin it down usefully?) and note the answer is no, because a useful map would be a group homomorphism Z/n -> Z/p, which is zero when gcd(n,p)=1. What remains untested is the non-homomorphic case.
smallest_experiment: On 20-26 bit curves: implement E(Z/p^k) arithmetic for k=2,3 (projective coordinates, since points can reduce to O); compute the canonical n-torsion lift of P by the projection R -> R - [n^{-1} mod p^k][n]R; then for all k in a large sample compute the higher p-adic digits d_1(x(kP-hat)), d_2(...) and run (a) a chi-square test of d_1 against k mod small m, (b) a Fourier test for correlation with additive characters of Z/n, (c) a test of whether d_1 is a homomorphism-like function. Pure Python with integers; no external libraries needed.
kill_criteria: DEAD if the higher p-adic digits of the canonical lift are statistically independent of k at the sqrt(sample) noise level for all k=2,3 and all toy curves -- which the splitting argument predicts. Also DEAD by proof: any efficiently computable homomorphism E(F_p) -> (Z/p^j, +) is zero since gcd(n,p)=1.
expected_complexity: None. The value is the closure: a measured negative plus a one-line proof kills the whole 'lift to a ring' family, including the recurring proposals to use Z/p^2 or Z/pq.
novelty_note: This is deliberately the audit of a known dead end, but the precise statement (canonical splitting from gcd(n,p)=1 plus the observation that lambda-equivariance does not break the splitting because lambda acts on E_1 by the unit beta-tilde - ell) is stronger and more reusable than the usual 'Smart's attack only works for trace one', and it generalizes to Z[omega]/pi^k where the CM might have been thought to help.

title: Encoding the discrete log in the zeta function of a bounded-genus auxiliary curve (Pila-computable transfer)
surface: 6 — transfer maps: transfer to an object whose invariants are computable in polynomial time
hypothesis: Point counting on curves/abelian varieties of FIXED genus over F_p is polynomial time (Pila), and a genus-g zeta function carries 2g numbers of size ~sqrt(p), i.e. enough bits to encode a 256-bit k; so the whole question is whether there is a bounded-degree algebraic construction C_{P,Q} whose Frobenius traces depend non-trivially on Q = kP rather than only on E.
nongeneric_structure: Polynomial-time computability of Frobenius traces for fixed-genus varieties over a PRIME field (Schoof/Pila/Adleman-Huang) -- an operation that has no generic-group analogue at all, since it reads the equation of a variety, not encodings. The CM structure supplies the natural bounded-genus candidates: the mu3 and mu6 covers of E and their twists by functions built from x(Q), y(Q).
prior_work:
[ESTABLISHED] Schoof 1985 for elliptic curves; Pila 1990 'Frobenius maps of abelian varieties and finding roots of unity in finite fields' (polynomial time for fixed dimension); Adleman-Huang for genus 2. [ESTABLISHED] the negative fact that must be circumvented: any construction depending only on the SUBGROUP generated by Q is constant in k, because n is prime so =

; and the Miller function with divisor k(P) - (kP) - (k-1)(O) has degree k, so the obvious encoding blows the genus up to ~k. SEARCH: 'discrete logarithm encoded in zeta function point counting auxiliary curve' — expected result: nothing; this is why I rate the construction step as the open part.
smallest_experiment: On 20-24 bit curves, take candidate families of bounded-genus curves whose coefficients are bounded-degree rational functions of (x(Q), y(Q)): e.g. the quadratic twist family y^2 = x^3 + 7 twisted by x(Q); the mu3 cover z^3 = f(x) with f built from x(Q); the genus-2 curve y^2 = (x^3+7)(x - x(Q)). For every k in [1,n), compute the trace of Frobenius by brute-force point counting (feasible at 20 bits) and build the map k -> trace vector. Measure (a) how many distinct trace vectors occur, (b) the maximum fiber size, (c) whether the map is efficiently invertible (e.g. monotone or lattice-structured) or looks random.
kill_criteria: DEAD if for every candidate family the map k -> trace vector has fibers of size Omega(n / p^(1/2)) with no exploitable structure (i.e. it behaves like a random function into a set of size ~sqrt(p)), meaning even a perfect inversion leaves sqrt(p) work -- which is no better than rho. Also DEAD if the trace vector turns out to depend only on the quadratic-residue class of x(Q) (a 1-bit leak), which is the most likely outcome.
expected_complexity: A win would need a family where k -> trace is injective and invertible, giving polynomial time; a partial win (trace determines k modulo a set of size p^(1/4)) would give 2^64. Both require the auxiliary curve's genus to stay bounded while its zeta function separates n values, and the counting argument (2g numbers of size sqrt(p) gives ~g*log(p) bits, enough for g>=1) says this is not ruled out by information theory -- only by the apparent impossibility of the construction.
novelty_note: This inverts the usual framing of transfer attacks. Instead of asking 'is there a homomorphism into an easy group', it asks 'is there a bounded-genus variety whose polynomially-computable arithmetic invariant depends on the point', which is a strictly weaker requirement (no homomorphism, no group structure needed) and which the generic group model cannot forbid. Even a clean negative -- a theorem that bounded-degree constructions from Q yield traces depending only on Q's image in E(F_p)/2E(F_p) -- would be a useful structural result.

title: Measured hardness exponent of bit-level ECDLP encodings, with p-shape / lambda / ladder ablations
surface: 7a - SAT/SMT bit-level encoding of kP=Q, treated as a measurement instrument rather than an attack
hypothesis: CDCL/bit-blasting on 'kP = Q' has an empirical cost 2^(c*b) for b-bit curves; the testable claim is that c drops measurably below 0.5 (rho's exponent) when the encoding exposes pseudo-Mersenne reduction (p = 2^k - 2^32 - 977) and the lambda-orbit symmetry. Expected honest answer: c >= 0.9 with astronomically bad constants, but the exponent has never been published with confidence intervals.
nongeneric_structure: The CNF/BV instance sees the F_p arithmetic circuit itself: carry chains of the multiplier and the fact that 2^256 = 2^32 + 977 mod p makes reduction a 3-term shallow adder tree instead of a general division; plus the j=0 endomorphism, which gives a 3-element solution orbit {k, lambda k, lambda^2 k} usable either as symmetry-breaking or as redundant clauses. A generic-group algorithm cannot see any of this, so a win here is not forbidden by Shoup/Nechaev; conversely a measured c >= 0.5 is evidence that CDCL fails to convert coordinate access into search reduction.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] Shoup 1997 'Lower bounds for discrete logarithms and related problems' (EUROCRYPT) and Nechaev 1994 give the Omega(sqrt n) generic bound. [ESTABLISHED] Bard, Courtois, Jefferson 2007, ePrint 2007/024, 'Efficient Methods for Conversion and Solution of Sparse Systems of Low-Degree Multivariate Polynomials over GF(2) via SAT-Solvers' - the standard algebraic-to-CNF route, reports exponential behaviour. SEARCH: 'Galbraith Gebregiyorgis summation polynomial algorithms elliptic curves characteristic two INDOCRYPT 2014' - should report SAT solvers used for point decomposition in char 2 and found competitive with Groebner only for tiny parameters. SEARCH: 'SAT solver elliptic curve discrete logarithm prime field measured scaling' - expect only anecdotal timings, no fitted exponent. WHAT IS DIFFERENT: the deliverable is a fitted exponent with bootstrap CIs plus a four-way encoding ablation, not a claim that SAT works; nobody has published the ablation that isolates whether the special prime shape helps at all.
smallest_experiment: PILOT ALREADY RUN IN THIS SESSION (scripts: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-virtualaquarium/e2bf485c-5536-57b5-8ef5-8e69bb3bcc7b/scratchpad/gencurves.py and .../satpilot.py). z3 5.1.0 bit-vector encoding of a double-and-add-always ladder over y^2=x^3+7, unknowns = scalar bits + one slope variable per step (slope encoded multiplicatively, s*(x2-x1)=y2-y1, so no inverses), width W = 2*ceil(log2 p)+4, reduction by URem. Correctness verified: recovered k re-multiplies to Q. Results: p=163, n=139 (8-bit): 67.7 s, 68.1 s, 52.1 s. p=547, n=547 (10-bit): 'unknown' at the 304 s timeout. For reference rho at 8 bits needs about 15 group operations (microseconds). So the measured growth is already >= 4.5x per 2 bits (c >= 1.1 bits^-1) with a ~10^7 constant penalty. FULL PROTOCOL: (1) generate y^2=x^3+7 curves with p = 1 mod 3 and prime order at b = 8,10,...,28 (gp/sympy, minutes); (2) four encodings - A: generic random prime; B: pseudo-Mersenne p = 2^k - c with reduction hand-circuited as shift+add+conditional-subtract instead of URem; C: B + lambda symmetry-breaking clause (lexicographic minimality over the orbit {k, lambda k, lambda^2 k} mod n); D: Montgomery x-only ladder instead of double-and-add-always; (3) back ends: z3 BV, and a custom bit-blaster feeding CaDiCaL/Glucose/CryptoMiniSat via python-sat (both installed here); (4) 20 random targets per cell, record median wall time AND median conflicts/decisions (machine independent); (5) robust linear fit of log2(conflicts) vs b with bootstrap 95% CI on the slope, per encoding.
kill_criteria: DEAD if the 95% CI lower bound of the fitted slope is >= 0.5 bits^-1 over b in [12,28] for all four encodings, or if ablations B/C/D shift the slope by less than 0.05 bits^-1 (i.e. the special prime and the endomorphism buy nothing structural). Also DEAD if the extrapolated crossover with rho lies beyond b = 60. Conversely, only a slope CI whose upper bound is < 0.5 and that is stable when the fit window is moved would keep it alive.
expected_complexity: Best case 2^(c*log2 n) with c < 0.5, which would require the instance to have a backdoor/strong-backdoor set of size o(b) so that CDCL's learned clauses effectively decide only o(b) of the scalar bits; there is no structural reason for that, and the pilot already contradicts it at 8-10 bits. Nothing here can beat rho unless c < 0.5 AND the per-conflict constant is within ~2^20 of a group operation.
novelty_note: Not a restatement of 'SAT is exponential': the output is a calibrated exponent + ablation table that (i) tells the rest of the programme exactly how much leverage bit-level reasoning gives on this curve family, and (ii) supplies the normalisation constant needed by the leakage-frontier idea. A published, CI-backed negative is itself usable; the folklore claim currently has no measured exponent attached.

title: Machine-searched structured factor bases over F_p, judged against a hard counting bound and a measured cost-per-relation exponent
surface: 7c + 7e - automated factor-base discovery and solver/Groebner-measured decomposition cost for prime-field Semaev systems
hypothesis: Over F_p there is no subfield, so the only candidate factor base is a structured subset S of F_p. A counting argument caps decomposition probability at |S|^m/(m! n) for ANY S, so 'far higher than random' as usually stated is impossible; the only live question is whether a machine-searched structured S (low-degree parametrisation, multiplicative coset, lambda-orbit-closed set, annealed union of intervals) makes the RESTRICTED Semaev system S_{m+1}(x_1..x_m, x_R)=0 with x_i in S cheap to solve - cheap enough that with m >= 5 the total exponent falls below 1/2.
nongeneric_structure: Semaev summation polynomials, i.e. the coordinate ring of E^m and the fact that x-coordinates of points summing to zero satisfy one explicit equation of degree 2^(m-1) - this is pure coordinate structure, invisible to a generic-group algorithm. Second non-generic hook: the integer ordering of F_p (intervals), which is not a group-theoretic notion. Third: j=0 lets S be closed under x -> beta x, so the system can be pushed into the ring of mu_3-invariants.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] Semaev 2004 ePrint 2004/031 'Summation polynomials and the discrete logarithm problem on elliptic curves'; Gaudry 2009 J. Symbolic Comput. 'Index calculus for abelian varieties of small dimension and the ECDLP'; Diem 2011 'On the discrete logarithm problem in elliptic curves' (Compositio) - the reason prime fields resist is precisely the absence of a Weil descent / subfield factor base. [ESTABLISHED] Faugere, Perret, Petit, Renault 2012 (EUROCRYPT) and Petit, Quisquater 2012 (ASIACRYPT) for the binary-field systems and first-fall degree analysis. [ESTABLISHED, high confidence] Faugere, Gaudry, Huot, Renault, 'Using symmetries in the index calculus for elliptic curves discrete logarithm', J. Cryptology 2014. SEARCH: 'Semaev 2015 ePrint new algorithm for the discrete logarithm problem on elliptic curves prime field interval factor base' - should be a proposal using x in a short interval over F_p, subsequently criticised for an over-optimistic count of solutions. SEARCH: 'Petit Kosters Messeng algebraic approaches elliptic curve discrete logarithm prime fields PKC 2016' and SEARCH: 'Amadori Pintore Sala discrete logarithm prime-field elliptic curves'. WHAT IS DIFFERENT: prior work fixes S by hand (an interval, or a subfield) and analyses; here S is the SEARCH VARIABLE, scored by a measured structure-ratio against the counting bound and by measured cost-per-relation, and the lambda-invariant symmetrisation specific to D=-3 is an ablation rather than an assumption.
smallest_experiment: Toy curves y^2=x^3+7, p = 1 mod 3, prime order, 20-32 bits (the repo already has such curves in /home/user/virtualaquarium/ecdlp/data/curves_raw.json and Semaev S_3,S_4 cached in /home/user/virtualaquarium/ecdlp/data/semaev/). Step 1 (cheap, hours): for m = 3,4,5 and |S| ~ n^(1/m), measure the empirical decomposition rate of 10^4 random points R for candidate S families - (a) interval [0,B); (b) union of k intervals optimised by simulated annealing directly on the measured rate; (c) multiplicative coset of a small subgroup of F_p^*; (d) image of x = f(t), deg f <= 4, t ranging over an interval; (e) any of the above closed under x -> beta x. Score = measured rate / (|S|^m/(m! n)) = 'structure ratio'. Step 2 (the real measurement): for the best few S, measure median time-to-one-relation with three engines - exhaustive over (x_1..x_{m-1}) plus root finding in x_m; z3 with x_i constrained to S (bit-vector range or explicit membership); sympy Groebner over GF(p) on the mu_3-symmetrised system, recording the maximum degree reached (first-fall / solving degree proxy). Step 3: fit log2(cost per relation) vs bits, and combine with n^(1/m) relations and sparse linear algebra (the repo already has a Wiedemann implementation at /home/user/virtualaquarium/ecdlp/csrc/wiedemann.c) into a TOTAL measured exponent; plot total exponent vs m.
kill_criteria: DEAD if (i) no searched S achieves a structure ratio above 1.2 (annealing converges to random-set behaviour), AND (ii) the fitted total exponent is >= 0.5 for every m in {3,4,5} across 20-32 bits. Additionally DEAD if mu_3 symmetrisation leaves the measured Groebner solving degree unchanged (then the j=0 structure contributes nothing beyond a factor 3) or if the cost-per-relation exponent for m=5 exceeds 1/5 by more than 0.05, which is the break-even the whole line needs.
expected_complexity: A real win needs m >= 5: |S| = n^(1/m) relations and sparse linear algebra n^(2/m) < n^(1/2) requires m >= 5, so decomposition must cost n^(1/5) amortised or less. For m=5 the Semaev polynomial S_6 has degree 16 per variable; for that to be solvable in time n^(1/5) the restricted system would have to be effectively triangular on S - that is exactly what must be true, and there is currently no candidate S for which it is. With m=3 the honest best case is n^(2/3), worse than rho.
novelty_note: Differs from the textbook 'index calculus does not work over prime fields' dead end in two ways: it states and uses the counting cap as a calibration baseline (so a 'high probability factor base' claim can be falsified in an afternoon rather than argued about), and it makes S the object of an automated search scored by measured relation cost at m=4,5 rather than a hand-chosen interval at m=3 where the answer is already known to be hopeless.

title: Exhaustive automated census of low-degree relations among x(P), x(lambda P), x(cP), x(P+cG) on j=0 curves
surface: 7b - automated conjecture discovery over the coordinate ring, as a rank computation rather than a solver search
hypothesis: On D=-3 curves, lambda acts on the x-line by the DEGREE-ONE map x -> beta x, unlike the generic case where the only automorphism acts trivially on x. If any mixed correspondence - e.g. the closure of {(x(P), x(lambda P + cG))} - has a vanishing polynomial of bidegree substantially below the generic c^2 growth of the c-th correspondence, that gives a cheap algebraic 'jump' relation that a descent could exploit. Test by exhaustive kernel search over the monomial basis.
nongeneric_structure: j=0 / CM by Z[omega]: End(E) = Z[omega] is rank 2, and the extra endomorphism is linear on x-coordinates. This is a statement about the coordinate ring of E and its correspondences, the most explicitly non-generic object available; a generic-group adversary has no coordinates and hence no ideal to census.
prior_work: [ESTABLISHED] Division polynomials / modular-like correspondences: the curve cut out by (x(P), x(cP)) has degree ~c^2, classical. [ESTABLISHED] Gallant, Lambert, Vanstone 2001 (CRYPTO) - GLV, uses exactly the degree-1 action of lambda on x for speed, never for an attack. [ESTABLISHED] Wiener & Zuccherato 1998 (SAC) and Gallant-Lambert-Vanstone 2000 (Math. Comp.) - automorphisms give only the sqrt(6) constant-factor rho speedup that defines THE BAR here. [ESTABLISHED, high confidence] Faugere, Gaudry, Huot, Renault 2014 (J. Cryptology) exploit symmetry of the factor base, but only symmetric-group/2-torsion symmetry of Semaev systems. WHAT IS DIFFERENT: this is an exhaustive bidegree census, run as rank computations over F_p on toy curves, covering MIXED lambda-and-translation correspondences that nobody has enumerated, with a j!=0 control curve to separate CM effects from generic ones. Also, checked this session: the secp256k1 CM data is itself unremarkable - t = p+1-n = 0x14551231950b75fc4402da1722fc9baef (129 bits, popcount 63) and 4p = t^2 + 3v^2 with v = 0xe4437ed6010e88286f547fa90abfe4c3 - so no low-weight trace to exploit; the hope must come from the correspondence degrees, not from t.
smallest_experiment: Toy curves 20-30 bits (repo curves reusable). For each pair of coordinate functions u, v drawn from {x(P), x(lambda P), x(cP), x(P+cG), x(lambda P + cG)} with c <= 16: sample N = 2 * (D+1)^2 random points P_i on the curve, build the matrix M[i, (a,b)] = u(P_i)^a v(P_i)^b for a,b <= D, and compute the rank over F_p by mod-p Gaussian elimination (numpy int64 with p < 2^31, or a 100-line C routine; the repo already links C libs via ctypes). Sweep D from 1 up to 40 and record the minimal D at which a kernel appears. Validate every discovered relation on 10^4 FRESH points and on a second curve with the same p but different generator, to exclude sampling artefacts. Run the identical census on a j != 0 control curve (y^2 = x^3 + ax + b with a != 0) and on random-map controls to calibrate false-discovery. Output: a table minimal-bidegree(c, twisted?) versus the theoretical c^2 prediction.
kill_criteria: DEAD if for every c <= 16 the measured minimal bidegree matches the classical prediction (c^2 up to the expected small constants) and the j=0 numbers differ from the j!=0 control only by the anticipated factor-3 orbit reductions. Also DEAD if any apparent low-degree relation fails to validate on fresh points or on a second base point (i.e. it was a rank artefact from insufficient N).
expected_complexity: A degree drop by a constant factor gives only a constant-factor speedup and does NOT beat rho. The only outcome that matters asymptotically is a family of correspondences whose degree grows like O(c) rather than Theta(c^2), which would allow a descent with polynomially many steps; for that to hold, the mixed lambda-translation correspondence would have to factor through a curve of genus far lower than expected - which would itself be a significant and checkable claim in arithmetic geometry.
novelty_note: This is conjecture DISCOVERY done as exhaustive linear algebra, not an attack; its value is a clean exhaustive negative table for the D=-3 case (a gap in the literature, where symmetry is always assumed to be the S_m/2-torsion kind), and a cheap positive-detection channel for anything the hand analysis missed. It is not a re-encoded generic search because the search space is monomials in coordinate functions, whose size is independent of n.

title: Heavy-Fourier-coefficient hunt over BIT-LEVEL coordinate functions, via sparse recovery and a learned f
surface: 7d - learnability/mutual-information, reformulated as a spectral measurement with a provable null
hypothesis: Predicting k from kP is information-theoretically trivial (the map is a bijection), so 'measure the mutual information' is the wrong experiment.
